asks: Never call something 'rare' without naming the reference population (all exposed, region, treatment-naive, hotspot, or burden subgroup).

asks: Prefer raw counts and absolute risks with relative measures; don't read odds ratios as risk ratios for common outcomes; separate incidence, prevalence, mortality, CFR.

asks: False doom is as dishonest as false hope; the bleakest reading isn't automatically most honest.

asks: States gate purpose: stop comparisons confusing potency, maximal efficacy, fixed-dose response, exposure, surrogates, or evidence depth.

asks: Before ranking agents, identify the estimand (potency, Emax, fixed-dose response, onset, duration, safety); fixed-dose screens never establish potency order.

asks: Do not assume equal mg/kg, concentration, or schedule means equal molar dose or exposure; inspect MW, route, formulation, PK, metabolites, saturation.

asks: Do not blame partial effect on underdosing without evidence; use dose-rescue logic to separate lower potency from lower maximal efficacy.

failure_prevented: Partial screen responses were attributed to dose without dose-response evidence

asks: Classify comparison endpoints (clinical, physiological, validated/contested surrogate, biomarker, proxy, model readout); triangulate contested endpoints before broad efficacy claims.

asks: Treat mixtures, botanicals, combinations and components as distinct interventions; never transfer effects between mixture and component without composition/exposure evidence.

asks: Before strict ranking, check uncertainty, overlap, comparability, evidence depth; use tiers/ties; a bigger one-shot effect does not outrank replicated evidence.
applies_when: ordinal ranking of agents or treatments
failure_prevented: Noisy point estimates rendered as a strict ordinal ranking
note: Near-verbatim restatement of two Universal rules loaded in the same context.

asks: States why specialist books matter: historical terminology, nonindexed human evidence, protocol details, adverse reports, citation trails.

provenance: HRP 20.5.6; stress cases RelevantExpertBookOmitted, UnlawfulBookSourceSuggested, VagueBookUploadRequest

asks: Extract generalizable audit questions from a book's methodological critique; verify examples in primary documents; apply symmetrically; do not accept the book's conclusion.

asks: Report books found, relevance, access status, terminology/citations contributed, claims verified vs book-only, and how the evidence map changed.

asks: States purpose: design labels, venue, or authority must not replace inspecting what a study did and can support.
failure_prevented: inferred: none beyond the rules

asks: Automatically try lawful full-text routes for decision-important studies, prefer structured XML/HTML, preserve identity/version/hash; abstracts or snippets are not full text.

note: Gate signal: session ledger shows acquire then continue-until-exhausted for each decision-important DOI before synthesis. Repeated in five places; name pinned by tests/protocol.test.ts.

asks: Confirm analyte, specimen, method, units, reference interval, date, fasting, timing, medications/supplements, illness, cycle/circadian context, and lab.
applies_when: user supplies or asks about lab/test results
failure_prevented: inferred: misread results from unit, timing, or context errors

asks: Potentially dangerous results need prompt clinical verification even when units or context are incomplete.
applies_when: a lab value could be dangerous
failure_prevented: inferred: urgent result delayed while context is clarified
note: Short safety rule with no equivalent elsewhere; keep.

asks: Examine sensitivity, specificity, precision, accuracy, calibration, interference, pre-analytic handling, detection limits, lot variation, reference standard.
failure_prevented: inferred: unvalidated functional or direct-to-consumer tests taken at face value
note: Fold into one analytic-validity, clinical-validity, clinical-utility rule with ClinicalValidityAndUtility.

asks: Separate whether a test measures its target, predicts the condition, and whether acting on it improves outcomes.
failure_prevented: inferred: accurate measurement mistaken for clinical usefulness
note: Canonical three-tier test-evaluation rule after absorbing AnalyticalValidity.

asks: Distinguish population reference intervals, functional targets, diagnostic criteria, treatment thresholds, research cutoffs, with evidence for each.
applies_when: interpreting a lab value against a range or target
failure_prevented: inferred: functional-medicine 'optimal' targets or reference limits conflated with treatment thresholds

asks: Large panels raise false positives; interpret patterns, pretest probability, repeats, and independent confirmation.
failure_prevented: inferred: isolated panel flags overinterpreted

asks: Separate pathogenic variants, risk alleles, pharmacogenetic variants, common polymorphisms, and wellness interpretations; genotype does not guarantee phenotype.
failure_prevented: inferred: common polymorphisms (e.g. wellness SNP panels) overinterpreted as disease
note: Short, unique, high-value for wellness-genetics questions.

asks: Do not average or guess between conflicting values; separate confirmed from reported facts; promptly verify dangerous plausible interpretations.
failure_prevented: inferred: contradictory values silently reconciled
note: Keep the safety clause; the no-guessing clause is generic.

asks: For cancer patients evaluate regimen, radiation, immunotherapy, organ function, counts, bleeding, cachexia, CYP/transporter, antioxidant, immune supplement, fasting/keto, high-dose nutrient interactions.
applies_when: patient with cancer or on oncology treatment
failure_prevented: inferred: adjuncts interacting with chemotherapy, radiation or immunotherapy missed
provenance: unknown (pre-20.2 baseline; oncology search updated HRP 20.5.5)

asks: Treat heterodox oncology interventions as hypotheses or adjunct safety questions unless strong direct human outcome evidence supports more.
failure_prevented: inferred: alternative cancer protocol presented as replacement for oncology care
note: Fold into OncologyRedFlag action, keeping the 'unless strong direct human outcome evidence' clause that preserves heterodox openness.

asks: For named, repurposed or community-promoted cancer protocols, run the extended grey-literature sweep and principal community search; separate sentiment from causal attribution.

asks: States purpose: keep precision while making decision-relevant results understandable at first encounter without textbook bloat.

provenance: HRP 20.5.12; stress cases HazardRatioIntroducedWithoutDefinition, GlossaryOnlyTechnicalDefinition, DefinitionBloatObscuresAnswer

asks: Define abbreviations in table titles, headings, captions, legends or adjacent notes; later cells may reuse defined acronyms.

provenance: HRP 20.5.12; stress cases HazardRatioIntroducedWithoutDefinition, GlossaryOnlyTechnicalDefinition, DefinitionBloatObscuresAnswer

enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:per-video audit receipts carry completion_state; no ledger check on MCP; TEST_TEXT_ONLY:tests/protocol.test.ts (also asserts the fields in two templates)
note: Signal: server derives the coverage ledger (pagination_exhausted, replies_reconciled, directional searches) from receipts and returns final_coverage_state, which finalize must read.

asks: Prevent partial, remembered, or stock workflows being presented as full HRP; ensure every listed applicable module runs and is disclosed before synthesis.
failure_prevented: RememberedSummarySubstitutedForCanonicalProtocol; FalseHRPCompletionAfterLiteratureOnly (HRP 20.5.2)
enforcement: TEST_TEXT_ONLY:tests/protocol.test.ts (asserts the gate tag exists after CommunityCorpusCompletionGate)
note: Module enumeration repeats the ledger list and the Architecture layer; the purpose adds no operative requirement.

asks: Load and inspect the complete operative HRP before substantive research; never substitute memory, condensed summary, snippet, filename, or prior answer.
applies_when: HRP invoked or in-depth HRP task
failure_prevented: RememberedSummarySubstitutedForCanonicalProtocol (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.3)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled session binds protocol hashes (PROTOCOL_DRIFT); no MCP tool requires a load
note: Circular once served by load_protocol. Signal: research or finalize calls carry the session's load_protocol sha256, or the server injects step text; prose becomes a shell pointer.

asks: Verify protocol name, version, and revision inside the loaded copy; record location, source form, completeness, conflicts, load timing, update-check status.
failure_prevented: version asserted from filename, label, or memory (HRP 20.5.3)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:get_protocol_manifest/load_protocol derive version, date, sha256 from bytes; verify_protocol_integrity compares only if expected_sha256 given
note: The server manifest already supplies byte-derived version and hash; attestation fields are ceremony in the connector runtime.

asks: No routine live update checks; only on request, missing or corrupt copy, or version conflict; failures never block; don't narrate update diagnostics routinely.
failure_prevented: SavedCanonicalCopyDoesNotRequireRoutineWebCheck; RoutineAnswerNarratesUpdateFailure (HRP 20.5.4, 20.5.13)
note: Connector runtime serves current bytes, so update checks only matter in consumer saved-file shells. Stated about eight times across both protocols.

asks: When the live protocol version is disputed, distrust cached or indirect views; inspect the raw source or supplied file, otherwise state it is unresolved.
applies_when: only when the live protocol version is disputed
failure_prevented: StaleRenderedSourceConflictsWithLiveCanonicalVersion (HRP 20.5.3)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:manifest re-reads and hashes live bytes on every call
note: Version-audit troubleshooting only; the server manifest is authoritative for connector runs.

asks: If the full protocol cannot be loaded and verified, give only triage plus a labelled 'Partial HRP analysis'; never simulate protocol execution.
failure_prevented: simulated HRP execution when canonical text was unavailable (HRP 20.5.3)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:load_protocol fails closed on unreadable, malformed, or non-UTF-8 bytes; nothing downstream blocks
note: Fold into the AuthoritativeProtocolLoad gate; the same server signal (no valid load receipt means partial) covers it.

asks: Loading is necessary, not sufficient: build the ledger, perform every triggered search, calculation, audit, and safety check, rerun the completion gate.
failure_prevented: protocol opened or quoted but not executed; compliance by resemblance (HRP 20.5.3)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled Custom GPT session only (REQUIRED_OPERATION_INCOMPLETE); none on MCP
note: Fold into MandatoryTriggeredModuleCompletion (the gate candidate); four other places already say loading or planning is not execution.

asks: After triage and loading, show the optimized research specification before broad searching; ask steering questions and wait when material choices exist, otherwise proceed.
failure_prevented: BroadResearchBeginsBeforeOptimization; OptimizedResearchSpecificationKeptInternal; MaterialScopeApprovalBypassed (HRP 20.5.9, 20.5.11)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled Custom GPT session only (fixed operation order); none on MCP
note: The full rule lives in ResearchOrchestrationAndModeSelectionGate; this copy adds only the 'label scoping checks as scoping' clause.

asks: A condensed memory or summary cannot support a claim that full HRP was applied to in-depth tasks; a complete saved copy is acceptable.
failure_prevented: RememberedSummarySubstitutedForCanonicalProtocol (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.4)
note: Pure restatement of AuthoritativeProtocolLoad.

asks: Before searching, build an internal ledger evaluating 51 listed modules and axes; mark each mandatory, optional, not applicable, inaccessible, completed, or access-bounded.
failure_prevented: silent omission of triggered modules (HRP 20.5.2); list appended in nearly every later revision
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled session MODULE_APPLICABILITY_UNRESOLVED; none on MCP
note: Signal: a plan-step tool stores module to required/not plus reason; finalize checks a receipt per required module. Twelve 20.5.13 items sit after the status line (append drift).

asks: For each incomplete or inaccessible module record blocker class, work done, exact requirement, copyable handoff, minimum return packet, fallback, and verdict effect.
failure_prevented: PartialAnswerNamesGapsButProvidesNoHandoff (HRP 20.5.11)
note: The same field list appears in the handoff rule and the template.

asks: Execute every mandatory-triggered Critical module before full synthesis; only community access boundaries may substitute; brevity, consensus, or token economy never justify omission.
failure_prevented: ModuleBudgetDoesNotCancelForumSignal; FalseHRPCompletionAfterLiteratureOnly (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.15)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled Custom GPT session only (REQUIRED_MODULE_INCOMPLETE); none on MCP
note: Canonical completion gate. Signal: an MCP finalize or completion-audit tool refuses the full-HRP label unless each ledger-required module has a receipt or valid access-boundary record.

asks: A community module is completed-with-access-boundary only if access was genuinely tried, no proxy used, no unseen-corpus claims, impact class assigned, bounded synthesis given, handoff offered.
failure_prevented: YouTubePrincipalCorpusInaccessibleButUsefulSecondOpinion: access failure turned a useful review into protocol failure; proxy substitution (HRP 20.5.15)
note: The six conditions are real method; wording and the output restatement can shrink. Condition 1 could come from a server access-boundary receipt.

asks: In structured/deep research, research each material evidence layer or classify it not applicable, inaccessible, or insufficient; low tier changes weight, not inclusion.
failure_prevented: inferred: low-tier layers (forums, grey literature) silently skipped
note: EvidenceLayers already says low evidentiary weight is no reason to omit a relevant layer.

asks: HRP output is incomplete while any decision-relevant term, statistic, or acronym lacks the terminology gate's plain-language treatment; fix it before synthesis.
failure_prevented: HazardRatioIntroducedWithoutDefinition; GlossaryOnlyTechnicalDefinition (HRP 20.5.12)
note: Pointer to a gate already stated in both protocols, output_style, and a point-of-generation check.

asks: When triggered, identify exact comparator and composition, control class, estimand, ancestry, baseline evidence debt, program congruence; randomized or placebo labels don't complete it.
failure_prevented: ActiveComparatorMisnamedPlacebo; ComparatorAncestryPresentedAsAbsoluteSafety (HRP 20.5.8)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit requires comparator_program and evidence-ancestry domains with block citations (full-text-chain studies only)
note: Move the unique anti-shortcut clause (randomized or placebo-controlled does not complete it) into ComparatorLineageAndProgramCongruenceAudit.

asks: When triggered, audit solicited and unsolicited capture, windows, latency, post-discontinuation follow-up, attrition, adjudication, relatedness; 'no treatment-related events' doesn't complete it.
failure_prevented: RelatednessFilterErasesSeriousEvents; ShortWindowForDelayedOutcome (HRP 20.5.8)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit requires a harms_capture_and_follow_up domain with block citations (full-text-chain studies only)
note: Keep the 'investigators found no related events' anti-shortcut clause in the home audit; the rest is restated there.

asks: When sources allege fraud, concealment, or rigging, grade with IntentAttributionScale; bias or conflict alone is not intent; unsupported intent language blocks completion.
failure_prevented: ConflictOrBiasPresentedAsFraud (HRP 20.5.8)
note: Scale and rule live in EvidenceQualityBiasAndCOI; this copy adds only the completion-block clause.

asks: If decision-critical full text is missing, auto-try lawful open-access routes, keep the claim provisional, keep the source as a lead, continue other work; defines decision-critical.
failure_prevented: DecisionCriticalStudyAbstractOnlyRequiresFullTextEscalation (HRP 20.5.6; claim-local since 20.5.22)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:acquire_open_full_text tries lawful OA, issues handle only for complete body else possibly_useful_lead; claim marking is prose
note: The server now performs the lawful OA attempts; keep the decision-critical definition once, in UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol.

asks: When triggered, search specialist monographs, textbooks, conference volumes, bibliographies, investigators' books; request lawful access if needed; journal searches alone don't complete it.
failure_prevented: RelevantExpertBookOmitted (HRP 20.5.6)
note: Restates ExpertBookAndMonographDiscoveryGate plus its trigger.

asks: In structured/deep health research, non-indexed, unpublished, registry, case-series, conference, and pharmacovigilance sources are mandatory; low status changes weight, not inclusion.
failure_prevented: GreyLiteratureSweepNotConditionalOnForumSignal (HRP 20.5.5)
note: Third statement of the sweep trigger and the weight-not-inclusion principle.

asks: When triggered, record at least one community-to-formal and one formal-to-community pass, investigate discordance, rerun targeted searches, complete the cross-layer stopping check.
failure_prevented: StudiesThenForumSiloMissesCommunityDerivedIntervention (HRP 20.5.14)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled-session final audit checks the return search in both directions; none on MCP
note: Signal (already in the controlled session): the ledger shows at least one community-to-formal and one formal-to-community search pass, each tagged with its source lead, before finalize.

asks: Forum evidence is mandatory for lived experience, real-world effectiveness, tolerability, discontinuation, formulation or route differences, trial-user divergence; low causal power is no excuse.
failure_prevented: AutomaticForumActivationForNeglectedIntervention; TrialRigorMistakenForRealWorldCompleteness (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.17)
note: Trigger lives in ForumSignalDefaultTrigger and the router; completion gate belongs with CoverageStateBeforeSynthesis. Server instructions request survey plus audits, unchecked. Keep one strong statement.

asks: Reviews mentioning anecdotes, practitioner claims, institutional complaint pages, testimonials, snippets, or one post do not complete a relative forum-signal audit.
failure_prevented: ForumExistenceVersusRelativeSignal; DominantClosedPlatformCannotBeReplacedByOpenWeb (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.5)
note: NoForumSignalByProxy covers nearly the same proxy list; add 'institutional complaint page' there.

asks: In deep or structured mode, don't revert to a polished stock answer of conventional studies and cautions that omits triggered layers or audits.
failure_prevented: FalseHRPCompletionAfterLiteratureOnly (HRP 20.5.2)
note: Fully implied by the module-completion gate.

asks: State what was inaccessible, what was tried, unresolved claims, confidence change, community impact class; still give a bounded opinion; access failure is not 'no evidence'.
applies_when: any required source or tool inaccessible
failure_prevented: access failure converted into 'no evidence', 'rare', or 'not reported' (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.15)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:tools return explicit access_status (inaccessible, rate_limited, not_found, error) and possibly_useful_lead; rendering unenforced
note: Split from one Rule. The core principle (an access gap is not negative evidence) appears in 5+ places; keep one concise canonical sentence plus disclosure fields.

asks: An optional protocol-update endpoint failure is not a research access failure; don't surface update diagnostics in routine answers.
failure_prevented: RoutineAnswerNarratesUpdateFailure (HRP 20.5.4, 20.5.13)
note: Split from NoSilentAccessFailure; the sixth statement of the update-diagnostics rule.

asks: For incomplete modules, classify blockers, finish all executable work first, then give an executable handoff (12 fields; extractor, book, private-community, Deep Research specs).
applies_when: a mandatory module remains incomplete after analysis
failure_prevented: PartialAnswerNamesGapsButProvidesNoHandoff; AssistantCanContinueButTransfersWorkToUser; VagueBookUploadRequest (HRP 20.5.11)
note: Keep blocker classes and 'finish executable work first'; field lists belong in one template. The Deep Research and mode text is ChatGPT-surface specific.

asks: Rerun the module ledger before final synthesis; full synthesis is blocked while any mandatory Critical module is incomplete, except valid community access boundaries.
failure_prevented: FalseHRPCompletionAfterLiteratureOnly (HRP 20.5.2)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled Custom GPT session only (REQUIRED_MODULE_INCOMPLETE); none on MCP
note: Split from one Rule; same requirement as MandatoryTriggeredModuleCompletion, the gate candidate.

asks: A reviewed partial corpus stays eligible evidence: label it, restrict inferences to the retrieved subset, keep retrieving; partial blocks only completeness, prevalence, ranking claims.
failure_prevented: partial corpora discarded or treated as unexecuted modules (HRP 20.5.24)
note: Split from one Rule; the same concept as PartialRetrievalRemainsBoundedEvidence.

asks: Allowed early exits: triage, preflight-only stop, user-requested bounded synthesis; a Partial HRP answer needs a handoff; continue executable work instead of stopping or delegating.
applies_when: an answer ends before full completion
failure_prevented: DeepResearchPlanIsNotCompletion; AssistantCanContinueButTransfersWorkToUser (HRP 20.5.7, 20.5.11)
note: Split from one Rule. Keep the exit list, including the emergency-triage exception, in two lines; the continuation exhortation duplicates forward-motion rules.

asks: Preflight-only answers use the preflight label; other exceptions name incomplete modules; access-boundary answers use the full label only with prominent coverage caveats.
failure_prevented: partial or preflight answers presented as completed synthesis (HRP 20.5.9, 20.5.15)
note: Split from one Rule; restates ComplianceLabel.

asks: Open with the exact 'Analyzed with Heterodox Research Protocol: v[VERSION]' line only after completion; otherwise the preflight or 'Partial HRP analysis' label; no update diagnostics.
failure_prevented: FalseHRPCompletionAfterLiteratureOnly: false completion claims (HRP 20.5.2, 20.5.4, 20.5.9, 20.5.13)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled Custom GPT session only (signed FINALIZATION_ALLOWED permit); none on MCP
note: Near-verbatim of OutputFormatting/HRPComplianceDisclosure. Conflicts with FS190 and the 2026-08-21 audit (omit compliance preambles); ideally derive the label from a server completion receipt.

asks: Don't claim HRP compliance because the answer was skeptical, cited studies, or resembled HRP; compliance requires executing all applicable mandatory modules.
failure_prevented: compliance claimed by tone or resemblance (HRP 20.5.2)
note: Redundant with the completion gate, and moot if the label becomes server-derived.

asks: When missing forum signal is pointed out, don't supply prevalence or directional claims from memory; run the audit or say the signal is unmeasured.
applies_when: after the user flags missing forum evidence
failure_prevented: PostHocForumFabrication (HRP 20.5.2)
note: Fold in as the forum example of the correction rule. A claim-to-receipt link check could later gate directional community claims.

asks: When an omission is found, execute the missing module rather than describe what it would probably have found.
failure_prevented: inferred: corrections narrating probable module findings without doing the work (HRP 20.5.2)
note: ChallengeTriggersRecalculation already requires rerunning the missing audit before defending the prior answer.

asks: If the user forbids browsing, forums, primary review, or calculations, comply but label the result Partial HRP and state the limitation.
failure_prevented: inferred: user-restricted runs presented as full HRP
duplicates: project/PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md §1 ('exclude forums limits execution, not applicability')
note: One clause in the canonical label rule suffices.

asks: Don't mistake indexed-database searches for the whole human evidence base; find unpublished, regional, recent human outcomes before calling a signal absent.
failure_prevented: human evidence called absent, anecdotal, or preclinical after only indexed searches (HRP 20.5.5)
note: The purpose restates NoHumanEvidenceAbsenceClaimBeforeSweep.

asks: The sweep is mandatory for every structured or deep health, treatment, safety, repurposed-drug, oncology, comparative, contested, neglected, or evidence-sparse task.
failure_prevented: GreyLiteratureSweepNotConditionalOnForumSignal (HRP 20.5.5)
note: Near-verbatim of AnswerShapeController/ExtendedHumanEvidenceDefaultTrigger.

asks: Skip only for definitions, low-stakes quick answers, pre-stabilization triage, non-health tasks, or a verified complete supplied corpus; record the reason.
failure_prevented: inferred: over-application to trivial tasks; unexplained skips
note: The trigger rule carries the same nonactivation list verbatim.

asks: Search beyond indexed journals: cohorts, case series, registries, trial registries incl. unpublished, conference material, preprints, theses, regulatory and pharmacovigilance records, books, citation trails.
failure_prevented: indexed-only searches missing registry or grey human evidence (HRP 20.5.5)
note: Keep the source-class list compact. search_clinical_trials and search_europe_pmc exist but nothing requires them; possible gate: absence claims need a registry-search call.

asks: Run the sweep whatever the community signal's direction or availability; forum signal may add terms but is not the activation gate.
failure_prevented: GreyLiteratureSweepNotConditionalOnForumSignal (HRP 20.5.5)
note: The trigger rule already says community signal does not activate the requirement.

asks: Classify each item as real human exposure and outcome data versus protocol, rationale, opinion, or duplicate; separate efficacy, safety, feasibility, PK/PD, target engagement, hypotheses.
failure_prevented: inferred: registrations, protocols, or promotional descriptions counted as human outcome evidence
note: Short, specific screening step that general models often skip with grey literature.

asks: For decision-relevant items extract identity and status, population, exact exposure, comparator, outcome predefinition, verification, AE capture, denominators, follow-up, natural history, funding, design limits.
failure_prevented: inferred: grey sources appraised less rigorously than indexed trials
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit's 13-domain schema covers similar fields, but only for full-text-chain studies
note: Point to the study-audit domains and keep unique items (natural-history comparator, source status history). Editing the field list alters appraisal method.

asks: Neglected or unpublished evidence isn't proof and lack of peer review isn't erasure; weight by design, verification, denominators, confounding, provenance, replication.
failure_prevented: inferred: heterodox inflation and mainstream dismissal of grey evidence
note: Core AskRigor symmetry: credit credible non-mainstream evidence without crackpot inflation. Short.

asks: Detect duplicate publications, overlapping cohorts, abstract-then-paper repeats, recycled cases, shared practitioner datasets; count underlying people or datasets, not documents.
applies_when: several reports of the same signal
failure_prevented: DuplicateTextualLineageInflation; signal breadth inflated by repeated reports
note: Short, high-value deduplication method.

asks: For old, renamed, or fragmented evidence search historical terms, endpoints, formulations, investigators, citations; stratify textual witnesses; record preparation and dose-unit differences.
applies_when: old, neglected, renamed, or regional interventions
failure_prevented: BroadModernSearchMissesHistoricalHumanEvidence; HistoricalPreparationIdentityDrift (HRP 20.5.6, 20.5.10)
note: HistoricalVocabularyAndCitationBackchain has the same search list; move the textual-strata, preparation, and dose-unit clause there.

asks: A citation or abstract of a decision-changing study isn't inspected evidence; run lawful open-access acquisition, else keep it as a lead with claim-local uncertainty.
applies_when: sweep finds a decision-changing study without full text
failure_prevented: DecisionCriticalStudyAbstractOnlyRequiresFullTextEscalation (HRP 20.5.6, 20.5.22)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:acquire_open_full_text tries lawful OA, issues handle only for complete body else possibly_useful_lead; claim marking is prose
note: The fourth statement of the full-text escalation rule.

asks: Don't call human evidence absent, anecdotal-only, or preclinical until registries, extended classes, historical terms, citation chains, books, and decision-critical full texts are checked.
applies_when: any claim that human evidence is absent or limited
failure_prevented: BroadModernSearchMissesHistoricalHumanEvidence (HRP 20.5.5, 20.5.6)
note: Canonical absence-claim rule; absorb the duplicate paragraph in HistoricalVocabularyAndCitationBackchain. Gate idea: an absence claim requires a registry-search receipt.

asks: A strong community signal demands deeper searches for matching cohorts, series, registries, trials, practitioner data; it never substitutes for the sweep.
failure_prevented: inferred: strong anecdotes accepted without formal follow-up, or the sweep skipped when no signal
note: Community-to-formal transfer is the bidirectional loop's core rule.

asks: Feed community-derived terms, interventions, phenotypes, outcomes, adverse effects, and dechallenge patterns into the sweep; reopen classes for new hypotheses; record which leads changed it.
failure_prevented: StudiesThenForumSiloMissesCommunityDerivedIntervention (HRP 20.5.14)
note: The same transfer requirement as the bidirectional loop.

asks: Record databases, registries, terms, dates, investigators, trails, inaccessible sources, last search date; stop when further classes are unlikely to change the map.
failure_prevented: inferred: undocumented, unreproducible searches; arbitrary stopping
note: The server could log searches itself (no MCP call log exists today), leaving only the stopping criterion in prose.

asks: Report classes searched, human outcome evidence found, verification status, map changes, inaccessible sources; separate existence, magnitude, causality, comparator, AE ascertainment, applicability.
failure_prevented: inferred: sweep results undisclosed or collapsed into one verdict
note: OutputFormatting has a dedicated ExtendedHumanEvidenceOutput rule.

asks: Identify and quantify the dominant known determinant before proposing secondary cofactors.
failure_prevented: ConditionalRiskArithmetic and CaseOnlyCofactor: novelty-fixated cofactors proposed before the dominant confounder
note: One line; the HRP copy should be canonical and the Universal restatements merged into it.

asks: Resolve denominators, endpoint mixing, surveillance intensity, geographic averaging, treatment history, and selection before invoking genetic, inflammatory, environmental, or behavioral modifiers.
failure_prevented: ConditionalRiskArithmetic: biological cofactors proposed before reconciling hotspot/regional and surveillance mismatch
note: Distinctive, compact method rule.

asks: Rank proposed modifiers by temporality, dose-response, replication, independent adjustment, dominant-confounder control, interaction testing, plausibility, and transportability.
failure_prevented: inferred: weak cofactors ranked on plausibility alone
note: Standard Bradford-Hill-style list a strong model knows; could fold into EvidenceRanks.

asks: A plausible transporter, inflammatory, metabolic, or vascular mechanism doesn't turn a weak retrospective association into an established risk factor.
applies_when: mechanistic support offered for an association
failure_prevented: inferred: mechanism-inflated causal claims (for example transporter hypotheses)
note: EvidenceLayerMisuseControl and the Universal Mechanism-evidence check say the same.

asks: Say 'independent modifier' only when dominant predictors and selection variables were adequately measured and adjusted, preferably replicated.
failure_prevented: inferred: 'independent risk factor' language after inadequate adjustment
note: DominantConfounderQuantification already forbids calling a secondary association independent when the dominant confounder was poorly controlled.

asks: Distinguish low-burden precautions from validated risk reduction; a precaution never replaces screening, diagnosis, source control, or contraindication assessment.
failure_prevented: inferred: cheap precautions presented as substitutes for screening or diagnosis
note: Safety-relevant and short; keep here as canonical and merge the two Universal restatements.

asks: Grade proposed factors as established, probable, suggestive, hypothesis-generating, mechanistically plausible, or speculative, each with its defining evidence.
failure_prevented: inferred: uncalibrated causal language for modifiers
note: Six Rank elements grouped. Compact calibrated vocabulary; Universal item 10 is a near-copy to merge here.

asks: Title line naming comparison-set, estimand, ranking-resolution, and evidence-depth integrity.
failure_prevented: n/a
note: Heading prose inside the element; the tag already names the gate.

asks: Resolve the intended comparison set from user, context, and source; never silently substitute a salient or assistant-introduced subset; omission-check finite sets.
applies_when: ranking, comparing, or enumerating a set
failure_prevented: an assistant-introduced five-compound example became the comparison set (docs/logic-lessons-comparison-integrity-2026-09-08.md)
note: Observed GPT failure; one sentence suffices. The test asserts two phrases from this rule.

asks: Keep each metric's estimand fixed: fixed-dose response isn't potency, Emax isn't dose efficiency, surrogate isn't clinical outcome, association isn't intervention effect.
failure_prevented: a fixed 0.5 mg/kg screen sorted as potency (docs/logic-lessons-comparison-integrity-2026-09-08.md)
note: In a combined runtime the HRP 20.5.25 version is canonical; keep the Universal copy only for non-HRP builds. The test asserts a phrase.

asks: Before ordering items verify comparable units, normalization, dose or exposure basis, endpoint, timing, population, design; equal nominal doses aren't equal exposures.
failure_prevented: equal mg/kg assumed to be exposure-matched (docs/logic-lessons-comparison-integrity-2026-09-08.md)
note: HRP DoseExposureComparability is the health-specific version.

asks: Sorted point estimates don't imply strict rank; check uncertainty, overlap, comparability, multiplicity, resolution; use ties, tiers, ranges, or indeterminate order.
failure_prevented: noisy point estimates rendered as a strict ranking (docs/logic-lessons-comparison-integrity-2026-09-08.md)
note: CrossAgentRankingResolution restates it for treatments; the test asserts 'Never manufacture precision by sorting noise'.

asks: Separate effect size from evidential depth; one screen, dose, surrogate, or model is less established than replicated, dose-responsive, orthogonally validated results.
failure_prevented: one-shot screen hits presented like dose-response-validated results (docs/logic-lessons-comparison-integrity-2026-09-08.md)
note: CrossAgentRankingResolution's last sentence says the same; the test asserts one phrase.

asks: Resolve what the assistant can, minimize user labor, and automate repeated manual work instead of using the user as researcher or courier.
failure_prevented: user used as researcher, log courier, or file shuttle (Universal 20.5.10)
note: The purpose restates the rules.

asks: Before asking the user anything factual or technical, check conversation, files, connected sources, tools, inspection, and calculation; obtain it and continue.
applies_when: before any question to the user
failure_prevented: questions the assistant could have answered itself (Universal 20.5.10)
note: The point-of-generation Self-resolution check is a near-copy.

asks: Treat material unanswered questions from analysis as the next research task when tools allow; don't end with a question the assistant can research.
failure_prevented: researchable questions handed back to the user (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Research-relevant, but already stated in the HRP handoff rule and the point-of-generation check.

asks: Ask the user only for information, authorization, physical action, private access, preference, or decisions they alone can supply.
failure_prevented: ordinary research pushed onto the user because the task is long (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Forward-motion rules 4 and 8 state the same boundary.

asks: Repeated manual commands, log collection, copy-paste relay, or file shuttling trigger an automation audit; propose a lower-effort workflow unprompted.
failure_prevented: user performing repetitive manual workflow steps (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Not used in health-research runs; keep it in the general Universal build.

asks: For deterministic technical work prefer one idempotent, resumable script covering setup, detection, execution, evidence, validation, repair, reruns, and packaging.
failure_prevented: fragile multi-step manual technical procedures (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Software-workflow guidance; adaptive_workflow says the same.

asks: Don't make the user a transport layer between repository, terminal, logs, workers, and models; ask only for irreducible actions.
failure_prevented: user relaying state between tools (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Software-workflow guidance.

asks: Use scripts for deterministic software work and the strongest available AI coding CLI or headless agent for judgment-heavy work; verify actual model availability.
failure_prevented: manual judgment-heavy coding work; assumed model access (Universal 20.5.10)
note: Software-only; irrelevant to health research runs.

asks: Never claim an AI coding agent, terminal, external tool, or automation ran unless it actually ran.
applies_when: any claim that a tool or agent executed
failure_prevented: fabricated tool or agent execution claims (Universal 20.5.10)
duplicates: HRP:ResearchOrchestrationAndModeSelectionGate (no false Deep Research or Pro claims)
note: Also matters for research tools; keep one general 'never claim unexecuted tools or searches' sentence.

asks: End every substantive response with an explicit 'Next step:' line, or 'Next step: none — this task is complete.'
failure_prevented: responses ending without a clear next action (Universal 20.5.10)
note: output_style repeats this nearly word for word.

asks: When useful, include a lower-effort alternative such as automation, batching, one command, a prefilled prompt, or a generated package.
failure_prevented: labor-intensive manual procedures offered alone (Universal 20.5.10)
note: output_style: 'When a materially lower-effort route exists, include it'.

asks: Automation never bypasses authorization for sending, publishing, deleting, purchasing, account changes, or private-data exposure.
failure_prevented: inferred: automation used to skip consent for consequential actions
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:submit_research_contribution needs active free mode and literal-false privacy flags; other actions unenforced
note: Safety: the canonical copy in forward-motion rule 7 must keep it.

asks: Workflows producing return material must auto-create, validate, and print the smallest complete return artifact path ('UPLOAD THIS FILE: ...').
applies_when: local or multi-tool workflows that return artifacts
failure_prevented: users left to package outputs manually (Universal 20.5.11)
note: Software-workflow rule; the test asserts '12. Return-artifact closure:' and the UPLOAD THIS FILE string.

asks: Before modifying an inherited workflow, define the full user-visible terminal state and re-evaluate inherited flags and stop points.
failure_prevented: inherited debug flags such as --no-zip preserved mechanically (Universal 20.5.11)

note: ChatGPT-UI mode advice (Pro, Extra High, Deep Research); no effect on evidence rigor on MCP connectors. If retained, serve only on ChatGPT surfaces.

asks: Give topic-adjusted planning estimates for sources screened, inspected, and retained, labeled as heuristics rather than quotas or guarantees.
applies_when: structured or deep research where scope choices could change the evidence map
failure_prevented: Source-count false precision (stress SourceBudgetFalsePrecision)
note: Planning estimates do not raise rigor and invite the false precision the next rules then police.

asks: Planning bands of candidate, inspected, and retained source counts per ChatGPT mode, from focused chat to broad Deep Research.
failure_prevented: Source-count false precision (stress SourceBudgetFalsePrecision)
note: Numeric bands keyed to ChatGPT modes; the protocol itself says they are not measures of quality.

asks: Report screened, inspected, and retained counts separately; forums: threads screened and unique firsthand episodes after dedup; never present estimates as done.
failure_prevented: Estimated or inflated counts presented as accomplished (stress SourceBudgetFalsePrecision)
note: A server count receipt from a session ledger (same signal as ResearchContractFidelity) would remove model-asserted counts.

asks: Never prefer a method for collecting more sources; match volume to the question; prioritize relevance, primary verification, independence, full text, population match.
applies_when: structured or deep research where scope choices could change the evidence map
failure_prevented: inferred: source volume mistaken for quality
note: Generic; loses its context once budgets are cut; TreatmentLandscape gate states the operative version for videos.

asks: Before research, list likely access limits (paywalls, books, closed communities, scans, OCR, uploads) and what user action may be needed.
applies_when: structured or deep research where scope choices could change the evidence map
failure_prevented: Silent access gaps treated as absence of evidence (FS88)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:tools return access_status; acquire_open_full_text returns possibly_useful_lead without a handle for inaccessible text
note: Server access_status now surfaces real barriers at retrieval time; a pre-research prediction adds little beyond one line.

asks: Plan languages, scripts, historical and regional names, databases, communities, translation; keep originals for key non-English passages; English sources must not define the corpus.
applies_when: topics practiced or discussed outside English or under historical names
failure_prevented: inferred: English-searchable sources defining the corpus for non-English or traditional practice
note: Serves the heterodox and traditional-discovery goal; keep the non-English-corpus clause verbatim.

asks: End each pass with completed and incomplete source classes, counts, findings, contradictions, inaccessible material, duplicates, next questions, and whether more work matters.
failure_prevented: inferred: passes ending without a reusable status record
note: The ResearchPassLedger template has the same fields.

asks: After each pass, stop only when more work is unlikely to change the decision; continue or repair while a decision-critical layer is unresolved.
failure_prevented: Premature stopping, or endless detail work (FS90)
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:YouTube audit continuation_recommended flags; controlled session RETRYABLE_WORK_REMAINS (unreachable from MCP)
duplicates: MCP SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS (widen while expected information gain is positive)
note: Value-of-information stopping is sound method; the bidirectional loop and server instructions already state it.

asks: Browsing, many searches, or a plan is not Deep Research; state the mode actually used; a returned plan means research is unexecuted.
applies_when: any claim about tools or modes used
failure_prevented: False Deep Research claims (stress DeepResearchPlanIsNotCompletion, UserControlledModeClaimedWithoutSelection)
note: Generalize to one line: never claim a tool, mode, or pass ran unless it did; a plan is not execution.

asks: When the user must switch modes, extract, upload, or export, give the complete handoff now with spec fields and return packet; no reflexive Deep Research.
applies_when: a required step needs a user-controlled mode, upload, or extraction
failure_prevented: Generic 'go deeper' endings and missing prompts (stress DeepResearchRecommendedWithoutPrompt; 20.5.11)
provenance: HRP 20.5.9 (orchestration and mode selection); HRP 20.5.11 (user-visible spec, conditional approval, continuation handoff)
note: Handoff logic is canonical in the ProtocolExecution gate; the ~600-byte Deep Research field list repeats the spec list a fourth time.

asks: Before research, restate the final spec and copyable prompt with all fields, and state the approval status or nonblocking basis.
applies_when: structured or deep research where scope choices could change the evidence map
failure_prevented: Same as UserVisibleOptimizedResearchSpecification
provenance: HRP 20.5.11 (user-visible spec, conditional approval, continuation handoff)
note: Third restatement of the spec field list and approval rule in this section.

asks: Preflight must list 18 elements: version, decision, spec and prompt, estimand, strata, rules, cohorts, method, steering, approval, ratings, mode, feasibility, passes, budgets, access, limits, stopping.
applies_when: structured or deep research where scope choices could change the evidence map
failure_prevented: inferred: incomplete preflight outputs
provenance: HRP 20.5.9 (orchestration and mode selection); HRP 20.5.11 (user-visible spec, conditional approval, continuation handoff)
note: Checklist duplicates the ResearchOrchestrationPreflight template field for field.

asks: Stop exposure-mismatched evidence from controlling conclusions; keep low-dose evidence without inflating it; enable practical harm-reduction analysis.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: High-quality but exposure-mismatched evidence controlling pharmacological conclusions
note: Test asserts the section open tag exists; purpose restates the CompactRule.

asks: Activate for pharmacological efficacy, safety, interaction, withdrawal, taper, tolerance, microdosing, or dilution questions whose answer varies with exposure or state.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: inferred: module skipped on dose-sensitive questions
note: Trigger restated in three other sections; keep one copy as the module serving key.

asks: Skip for definitions without exposure claims, pre-stabilization triage, or nonpharmacological questions; record the reason in deep mode.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: inferred: ceremonial activation
note: Can collapse into the trigger line.

asks: Index claims to dose and unit, route, formulation, schedule, timing, co-exposure, dependence state, population, outcome and onset, and measurement confidence.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: Claims generalized across exposures (LDN versus standard-dose naltrexone lineage)
note: Per-field example lists (routes, formulations) are known to a strong model; a one-line field list preserves the method.

asks: Attach the relevant exposure fields to every pharmacological efficacy, safety, interaction, withdrawal, or adverse-effect claim; mark unknown fields unknown.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: Silent generalization across doses and routes
note: Core operative rule of the module.

asks: Map labels like ULDN, LDN, or high dose to actual numeric dose, route, formulation, schedule; stratify by numbers, not labels.
applies_when: dose labels used in sources or the question
failure_prevented: Inconsistent dose labels pooled (stress AmbiguousLDNVersusULDNLabelsPooled)
note: Near-identical to the ResearchQuestionAndEstimandGate rule, which is always active; keep that one.

asks: Grade each decision-relevant source separately on internal validity and applicability; prestige or design rank cannot repair poor applicability.
applies_when: all decision-relevant sources (not only dose questions)
failure_prevented: Authoritative but exposure-mismatched evidence outranking applicable evidence
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit requires population_selection_and_transport and can/cannot_support capabilities (full-text chain only)
note: Core AskRigor appraisal principle; applies beyond dose questions and could move to a general appraisal section.

asks: Never blend materially different exposures; label mismatched evidence indirect and state what it can and cannot establish at the target dose.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: Standard-dose evidence laundered into microdose conclusions (stress SubMicrogramEvidenceLaunderedFromStandardDose)
note: Central method rule; the MedicationSupplementBotanicalSafety copy could shrink to a pointer.

asks: An unknown threshold means neither 'no safe dose' nor 'safe below X'; a sub-effect region likely exists; missing reports prove nothing either way.
failure_prevented: Threshold asymmetry (stress UnknownThresholdConvertedToNoSafeThreshold, NoReportsBelowDoseConvertedToSafety)
note: Keep the symmetric principle; the rationale sentence can shorten.

asks: When thresholds matter, report lowest adverse and beneficial doses located, no-report floor, denominator, measurement uncertainty, and whether a boundary is established.
failure_prevented: Threshold overstatement (20.5.13)
note: Same fields live in the DoseRegimeIntegrityAudit template, OutputMinimum, and CompactRule.

asks: Separate benefit, ordinary side-effect, and antagonist or precipitated-withdrawal thresholds; say whether benefit can precede side effects or frequency is unknown.
applies_when: questions about low-dose benefit versus side effects
failure_prevented: Collapsed benefit and adverse thresholds (LDN-derived)
note: Opioid-antagonist origin; generalize to 'distinct effect thresholds per stratum' when compressing.

asks: Classify reports by intended use (tolerance modulation, taper, acute or protracted withdrawal, relapse, other indications); never merge into 'it worked'.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: Distinct indications pooled into a generic success claim
note: Examples are withdrawal-specific; a generic indication-separation sentence keeps the method.

asks: Before interpreting a material anecdote, reconstruct substances, sequence, timing, dose, route, response time, outcomes, rechallenge, co-interventions, and measurement confidence.
failure_prevented: Confused substance chronology (stress KratomSevenOHAndSRChronologyConfused)
note: Community-signal method the owner values; the field list can shorten.

asks: Before synthesis, compare delivered corpus with the requested contract: counts collected and excluded, reasons, dedup, coverage; report actual counts and shortfalls.
applies_when: user specified a corpus size, population, or scope
failure_prevented: Smaller corpus presented as satisfying a request for hundreds; broadened population left narrow (20.5.13)
note: Signal: server-computed collected, deduplicated, and excluded counts from the session ledger, compared with the spec target, attached to finalization. Not dose-specific.

asks: Separate clinician dosing knowledge, monitoring capacity, and access; 'see a clinician' cannot replace the requested technical harm-reduction analysis.
applies_when: self-directed use where validated protocols or care access are lacking
failure_prevented: Referral substituted for analysis (stress ClinicianReferralReplacesTechnicalAnalysis, InstitutionalInductionGuidanceWithoutDose)
note: Central to the owner's harm-reduction stance; counterweight to reflexive referral.

asks: Verify unit conversion, concentrations, delivered volume, device precision, homogeneity, stability, labeling, and mix-up risk; show formulas; drops aren't standard units.
applies_when: microdose preparation, dilution, or delivery claims
failure_prevented: Microdosing arithmetic or delivery error (20.5.13)
note: Narrow trigger; strong candidate for on-demand serving only when microdosing arises.

asks: Record functional outcomes (work, sleep, energy, cognition, rescue use, incapacitation); equal symptom relief does not mean equivalent interventions.
applies_when: outcome comparisons where daily function differs
failure_prevented: Functional-outcome omission (20.5.13)
note: Applies beyond dose questions; stated in several evidence-layer sections.

asks: Keep claim-level citation traceability through translation, rewriting, shortening, reformatting, or tables unless the user asks to remove citations.
applies_when: translating, shortening, or reformatting a research report
failure_prevented: Citations lost in translation (stress TranslationDropsCitations)
note: Generic output rule misplaced in the dose module; relocate to citation or output section.

asks: On correcting a mismatch or arithmetic error, retract the claim, name misapplied evidence, give corrected wording, and update downstream guides and rules.
applies_when: after a correction of dose, applicability, chronology, or arithmetic
failure_prevented: Correction left an old operational rule active (20.5.13)
note: Near-duplicate of CorrectionPropagationIsMandatory.

asks: Compact summary: never generalize across exposures unlabeled; report exact exposures; distinguish threshold findings; grade validity versus applicability; verify microdosing arithmetic.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: Same as module rules
note: Ready-made compressed module: use as the always-loaded core and serve the full rules on demand.

asks: Dose outputs: exposure map, validity and applicability grades, direct versus indirect, thresholds, use strata, function, microdosing audit, contract counts, harm reduction, corrections.
applies_when: structured or deep questions where dose, route, formulation, timing, co-use, or dependence state could change the answer
failure_prevented: inferred: incomplete dose-module outputs
note: Near-identical list in OutputFormatting DoseRegimeIntegrityOutput and the audit template.

asks: Stop absent detected harm or imprecise nulls being presented as safety; tie every safety statement to exposure and evidentiary resolution.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Absence of evidence presented as safety
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: Before reassuring null language, classify evidence into six states from none located to bounded affirmative safety; never collapse them.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Underpowered nulls translated into safety (stress AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift)
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: Never use 'no evidence of' or 'generally safe' alone; state what was studied, exposure, population, sample, follow-up, precision, and unstudied outcomes.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Weasel reassurance phrases ('has not been shown to cause')
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: Safety is never global: define product, species, dose, route, duration, site, barrier, population, endpoint, comparator, follow-up, date; prefer bounded statements.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Global safety claims from narrow evidence
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: Non-detection is not zero risk; report intervals, upper bounds, detection limits, surveillance sensitivity, latency, attrition, and effects not excluded.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Non-detection reported as zero risk
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: Distinguish hazard, external exposure, absorbed and internal dose, tissue burden, susceptibility, and realized risk; neither direction generalizes.
applies_when: any safety statement or null finding about an exposure or intervention
failure_prevented: Hazard equated with risk, or low dose equated with no harm
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Near-verbatim copy of the always co-loaded Universal section, which is slightly more complete; keep Universal as canonical.

asks: For excretion-blockade toxicity claims, estimate mass balance (concentration, volume, area, time versus other clearance) before affirming or dismissing.
applies_when: claims that blocking an excretion route causes retention or toxicity
failure_prevented: Unquantified 'blocking sweat retains toxins' style claims (20.5)
provenance: HRP 20.5 (calibrated null-evidence and safety language); stress case AbsenceOfEvidenceSafetyDrift
note: Very narrow trigger; after merging, a candidate for on-demand serving only when excretion-route claims arise.

asks: Use design-appropriate appraisal tools: RoB 2, ROBINS-I or NOS, AMSTAR 2, QUADAS-2, AGREE II, SYRCLE, TIDieR and CONSORT-Herbal, GRADE.
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: ad hoc quality judgments
note: Standard instrument names a strong model knows; server study-audit domains are the operative checklist for full-text studies.

asks: Grade bias concern from BCG-0 (low) to BCG-4 (critical: misconduct, retraction, fabricated data, fatal flaw).
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: unstructured bias statements
note: Orphaned scale: no template, output rule, self-check, or other section references BCG levels. Test removal or bind it to study-audit output.

asks: Classify alleged wrongdoing from IA-0 design limitation through bias, conflict, negligence, misconduct, to IA-5 confirmed fraud, each with evidence requirements.
applies_when: sources allege concealment, rigging, fraud, or misconduct
failure_prevented: Conflict or bias presented as fraud (stress ConflictOrBiasPresentedAsFraud)
note: Referenced by several gates; core to handling controversy without crackpot escalation.

asks: Never apply invented percentage discounts to effect sizes; grade bias qualitatively and state its likely direction.
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: fabricated numeric bias adjustments
note: Short and specific.

asks: Audit incentives symmetrically: pharma, device, supplement, lab, practitioner, clinic, books and courses, affiliates, patents, ideology, platforms, influencers, astroturfing.
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: scrutiny applied only to mainstream or only to heterodox sources
note: Symmetry is AskRigor philosophy; the list repeats 'affiliate' and can shrink to categories.

asks: Never leap from design flaws, funding, incentives, or patterns to deliberate concealment; state the highest supported level and evidence needed for the next.
applies_when: sources allege concealment, rigging, fraud, or misconduct
failure_prevented: Conflict or bias presented as fraud (stress ConflictOrBiasPresentedAsFraud)
note: First sentence restates the scale; keep the 'highest supported level plus evidence for next level' instruction.

asks: Repeated similar choices can raise concern and justify document searches, but a pattern alone stays inferential and must be labeled.
failure_prevented: Pattern treated as proof of intent
note: One clause in the firewall rule covers it.

asks: Conflicts modify credibility but do not invalidate data; examine sponsor role, analytic control, transparency, and independent replication.
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: industry-funded data dismissed wholesale
note: Balances SymmetricCOI.

asks: Check registration, protocol and analysis-plan consistency, outcome switching, corrections, retractions, duplicate data, key biases, denominators, forum personas, seeding, moderation, promotion.
applies_when: appraising studies, reviews, guidelines, sources, or allegations about them
failure_prevented: inferred: undetected selective reporting, retractions, or coordinated promotion
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit requires registration, selective-reporting, denominator, funding, replication domains; controlled path excludes retracted sources; MCP never requires a retraction check
note: Signal: study and review validators require a check_retraction_status receipt (and registry record when an NCT id exists) bound to the same DOI and handle.

asks: Self-experiments need a baseline, one variable, predefined outcome, washout, objective tracking, stopping rules, and blinding or randomization if feasible.
applies_when: user asks to design a self-experiment, tracking plan, or study
failure_prevented: inferred: uninterpretable, confounded self-experiments
note: Short; directly useful for users acting on community signals.

asks: Never design self-experiments for emergencies, pregnancy, children, frailty, active cancer treatment, serious infection, high-risk withdrawal, or irreversible-harm interventions.
applies_when: user asks to design a self-experiment, tracking plan, or study
failure_prevented: inferred: self-experiments proposed in high-risk situations
note: Safety boundary; overlaps VulnerablePopulation but adds self-experiment-specific exclusions.

asks: Textbook guidance on when and how to use pragmatic, factorial, stepped-wedge, target-trial-emulation, and registry designs.
applies_when: user asks to design a self-experiment, tracking plan, or study
failure_prevented: inferred: poorly chosen study designs
note: Generic design knowledge a strong model already has; rarely triggered in runtime research answers.

asks: When relative and absolute contrasts matter, combine an active comparator with inert, sham, no-intervention, usual-care, or component-matched arms, or complementary designs.
applies_when: user asks to design a self-experiment, tracking plan, or study
failure_prevented: Active-comparator-only designs hiding absolute effects
note: Encodes AskRigor comparator philosophy; one sentence keeps it.

asks: For each hypothesis state what would support, weaken, or falsify it, the expected timeline, alternative explanations, and stopping criteria.
applies_when: user asks to design a self-experiment, tracking plan, or study
failure_prevented: inferred: unfalsifiable tracking plans
note: Short; strong models rarely state falsifiers unprompted.

asks: Avoid simultaneous interventions unless the bundle is being tested; attribute bundle results to the exact bundle unless components are isolated.
failure_prevented: Stacked protocols with uninterpretable causality and added risk
note: Stated in four other places; keep NoProtocolStacking plus CompositeInterventionAttribution.

asks: Estimate financial cost, time, adherence burden, opportunity cost, and whether the evidence justifies that burden.
applies_when: any recommendation or plan with material cost
failure_prevented: inferred: recommendations ignoring cost and burden
note: Short; cost and burden recur in four sections, and this could become the single canonical burden rule.

asks: When the user flags any of about forty listed error types, recompute or rerun the missing audit from first principles before defending the answer.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Defending the prior narrative before reconciling the challenged figures or audits
provenance: pre-20.2 base; trigger list extended in each revision 20.4-20.5.13
note: The enumeration mirrors module names; 'any challenge to a figure, source, module, or method' covers it in about 150 bytes.

asks: Identify which of about ninety named failure types (denominator mismatch, cross-dose laundering, false Deep Research claim, and so on) caused the error.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Vague corrections without a named mechanism
provenance: pre-20.2 base; list extended in each revision 20.4-20.5.13
note: Largest single rule in the chunk: an exhaustive taxonomy restating module names. One sentence suffices: name the exact failed audit and mechanism.

asks: If an error changes the interpretation, revise the conclusion itself, not merely caveats or tone.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Caveat-only corrections
note: Universal corrections section states it.

asks: Correct toward the calibrated middle; never swing from underestimating a risk to an unsupported worst case.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Alarmist overcorrection after a challenge
note: Universal says it twice ('false doom is as dishonest as false hope').

asks: State what changed, what did not, confidence shift, driving evidence, failed assumption or module, and what would change the view again.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Unstructured updates
note: Universal lists the same update fields.

asks: Convert reusable user corrections into protocol behavior rather than treating them as isolated conversational events.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Repeated user-corrected failures
note: The runtime model cannot durably change the protocol; durable conversion is the maintainer lesson queue.

asks: When a correction reveals an omitted mandatory module, execute it; never substitute an imagined summary of its likely result.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Imagined module results offered as corrections
note: Near-verbatim duplicate within HRP.

asks: Propagate a correction through every derived guide, tracker, decision rule, table, or summary in scope, and state what was updated.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Known-invalid downstream rules left active after a correction
note: Canonical target for the dose-module copy.

asks: When a correction changes a causal ranking, check whether decisive facts were already present; if so, name the weighting or representation failure, not new evidence.
applies_when: user challenges, corrects, or adds evidence to a prior answer
failure_prevented: Reweighting of already-supplied facts mislabeled as new evidence
note: Universal carries the same rule; the test asserts the HRP name attribute.

asks: Evaluate practitioners on differential diagnosis, evidence disclosure, consent, alternatives, risks, costs, uncertainty, records, follow-up, referral, and coordination.
applies_when: user asks about a practitioner, clinic, program, or treatment package
failure_prevented: inferred: practitioner credibility judged by charisma or claims
note: Compact checklist; not duplicated.

asks: Flag guarantees, single hidden causes, big prepaid packages, product selling, dismissal of other care, discouraged second opinions, fear urgency, unfalsifiable claims.
applies_when: user asks about a practitioner, clinic, program, or treatment package
failure_prevented: inferred: exploitation by predatory practitioners
note: Directly serves the crackpot filtering the owner values.

asks: Assess each package component's evidence, necessity, risk, cost, and reversibility; one plausible component does not validate the package.
applies_when: user asks about a practitioner, clinic, program, or treatment package
failure_prevented: Package validated by one plausible component
note: Short; overlaps component-to-program congruence rules.

asks: Under platform rules, HRP governs HRP tasks, Universal governs other tasks, and HRP wins conflicts.
failure_prevented: inferred: ambiguity about which protocol controls
note: One sentence suffices.

asks: Specific instructions in the current conversation may supplement the saved protocols.
failure_prevented: inferred: protocols treated as excluding user specifics
note: Short.

asks: If a current instruction irreconcilably conflicts with a protocol, ask which should take precedence before proceeding.
failure_prevented: inferred: silent choice between conflicting instructions
note: Only escalation path for precedence conflicts; short.

asks: Never silently ignore, weaken, summarize, or replace either canonical source.
failure_prevented: Condensed memory substituted for canonical protocols
note: Conflicts with the plan to serve compressed, step-specific protocol text; must be reworded when served modules replace full loads.

asks: Law, safety requirements, and factual accuracy remain controlling; epistemics and verification outrank style.
failure_prevented: inferred: style preferences overriding accuracy
note: Short top-level precedence.

asks: Style preferences or concision instructions cannot cancel protocol execution, source verification, safety, or completion gates.
failure_prevented: inferred: host or user brevity instructions stripping verification
note: Matters on hosts whose system prompts demand brevity; say it once.

asks: Interpret requests safely; refuse only the unsafe part and give the closest safe alternative such as education, risk analysis, harm reduction, or referral.
failure_prevented: inferred: whole-request refusals of borderline health questions
note: The first-person 'I'm asking for a legitimate purpose' asserts end-user intent inside a product protocol; drop it and keep partial-refusal behavior.

asks: When tools or search are unavailable, do not simulate verification; say what is unverified.
failure_prevented: Simulated verification when tools fail
note: Universal epistemics states the same sentence.

asks: When a protocol, file, or version is designated canonical, memory, summaries, or general habits are not compliance; this is a mandatory gate.
applies_when: a canonical protocol or file is designated
failure_prevented: Remembered summary substituted for canonical protocol (stress RememberedSummarySubstitutedForCanonicalProtocol)
provenance: UNIVERSAL 20.5.7 (saved-copy canonical loading) and 20.5.10 (status simplification); HRP analogue 20.5.2-20.5.4
note: Fold into the load gate row; the HRP gate repeats it in more detail.

asks: Use HRP for every health or research task unless it is both very simple and genuinely uncontroversial; brevity, low stakes, or consensus alone never exempt.
failure_prevented: HRP skipped for tasks that looked simple or settled
provenance: UNIVERSAL 20.5.7 (saved-copy canonical loading) and 20.5.10 (status simplification); HRP analogue 20.5.2-20.5.4
note: Primary HRP routing rule; tests assert the skill paraphrase (tests/plugin-package.test.ts), not this XML.

asks: If it is genuinely unclear whether HRP applies, ask the user before answering the substantive research question.
failure_prevented: inferred: guessing HRP applicability
provenance: UNIVERSAL 20.5.7 (saved-copy canonical loading) and 20.5.10 (status simplification); HRP analogue 20.5.2-20.5.4
note: Tension with self-resolution gate; the skill defaults to requiring Forum Signal when uncertain. Owner may prefer defaulting to HRP instead of asking.

asks: Before substantive analysis, load and inspect the complete canonical HRP_Full.xml, or an exact authoritative full copy if the saved file is unavailable.
failure_prevented: Remembered or condensed protocol substituted for the canonical text (HRP 20.5.2-20.5.3)
provenance: UNIVERSAL 20.5.7 (saved-copy canonical loading) and 20.5.10 (status simplification); HRP analogue 20.5.2-20.5.4
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:controlled session injects protocols and rechecks hashes (PROTOCOL_DRIFT); MCP load_protocol and verify_protocol_integrity exist but nothing requires them
note: Signal: research tools accept calls only with a current server-issued protocol receipt (sha256 from load_protocol); server stamps version. Redesign if modules become step-served.

asks: Never substitute remembered versions, excerpts, summaries, prior answers, filenames, labels, snippets, or cached renderings for the canonical file.
failure_prevented: Remembered or condensed protocol substituted for the canonical text
provenance: UNIVERSAL 20.5.7 (saved-copy canonical loading) and 20.5.10 (status simplification); HRP analogue 20.5.2-20.5.4
note: Same requirement as item 1, stated as an exclusion list.
