asks: Report absolute risks and raw counts; translate ORs cautiously; separate observed from modeled; don't confuse RR, odds, incidence, prevalence, mortality, case-fatality.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: OddsRatioCommonOutcome
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Condenses four HRP rules.

asks: Check the dominant risk variable was measured with enough resolution; binary indicators may fail; check geography, age, sex, prior treatment, intensity, surveillance.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Binary burden adjustment misread (WholeReportNoveltyBias)
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP DominantConfounderQuantification.

asks: First exposure, geography, sex, age or behavior may predict without independent causation; state what was adjusted and what remains entangled.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Risk markers treated as causes
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Third copy of marker-versus-cause.

asks: Rank cofactors: established, replicated independent modifier, suggestive, hypothesis-generating, mechanistically plausible but weak, speculative.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Novel cofactors elevated without evidence grading
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP CofactorAndMechanismAudit EvidenceRanks.

asks: Require dose-response, temporality, replication, controls, dominant-confounder adjustment and cross-design consistency before treating a cofactor as real.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Plausible cofactors accepted on mechanism alone
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP cofactor evidence requirements.

asks: Determine whether a number came from a case definition, observed lower bound, model curve, operational screening rule or validated safety strategy.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: ThresholdPurpose
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP ThresholdPurposeAudit.

asks: Verify the primary paper behind each decisive claim; don't accept a later paper's 'confirmed' without checking the earlier report.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Citation-chain drift
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP CitationChainAudit.

asks: Absence of obvious symptoms doesn't exclude high burden where asymptomatic high burden is documented; use validated objective measures.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: AsymptomaticHighBurden
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP SymptomsAreNotAQuantitativeScreen and health_labs.

asks: A low-burden precaution (avoiding a possible cofactor) never replaces screening, measurement or contraindication management backed by stronger evidence.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Weak precautions displacing validated screening
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Safety content preserved in HRP PrecautionVersusValidatedControl.

asks: When evidence changes the view, state what changed, what didn't, confidence shift, driving evidence and what would reverse it.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: inferred: opaque belief updates
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Same update structure appears in corrections_and_calibration.

asks: When prior analysis mixed denominators, populations, endpoints or designs, name the exact mismatch instead of softening wording.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Corrections that soften tone without fixing substance
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP NameExactFailure.

asks: Audit the whole evidence package, not just the novel detail: strongest findings, weakest claims, central uncertainty, practical conclusion.
applies_when: surprising scientific, medical, epidemiological, safety or treatment-risk claims
failure_prevented: Novelty fixation on a user-highlighted cofactor (WholeReportNoveltyBias)
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Duplicates HRP WholeReportAudit.

asks: With sparse evidence give the most defensible bounded claim rather than invented precision, while stating clearly what the evidence establishes.
failure_prevented: inferred: false precision or vague non-answers from sparse data
provenance: unknown (Universal baseline; parallels the HRP 20.4 quantitative audit)
note: Covered by HRP SparseEventRule and null-evidence rules.

asks: States purpose: no intervention is recommended or ranked before its patient-specific conflicts are identified, graded, and resolved.
applies_when: any patient-specific intervention recommendation or ranking
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001-type failure: efficacy ranking before patient-specific contraindication review
note: Purpose restates the rules; fold into a one-line gate heading.

asks: Apply safety reconciliation before ranking to every candidate intervention of any type and any origin (user, guideline, research, community, assistant).
failure_prevented: inferred: assistant- or guideline-sourced candidates skip the safety review applied to user-proposed ones
note: Exhaustive intervention-type list compresses to 'every candidate, any source'; test asserts several listed words, so update it.

asks: Cross each candidate against diagnoses, current medications/supplements/exposures, allergies, organ function, reproductive context, and class contraindications; mark each known/unknown/not applicable.
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: patient's idiopathic intracranial hypertension not reconciled against retinoid candidates
note: Same field list repeats in the section Template and FS204; keep one list, ideally as a server-side schema.

asks: Treat missing safety inputs that could change suitability as unresolved; no patient-specific recommendation until obtained, shown irrelevant, or safely conditional.
failure_prevented: inferred: absent medication or allergy history treated as 'no conflict'
note: Natural validator rule: a material unknown field forces admission=no unless the output is flagged conditional.

asks: No patient-specific recommendation, preference, or efficacy rank until each material conflict or unknown resolves (compatible/avoid/modify/monitor/review); unresolved keeps admission at no.
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: retinoid ranked by efficacy despite unreconciled patient-specific conflict
note: Signal: validator receives one reconciliation record per ranked candidate; controlled finalize stays BOUNDED_NONRANKING_ONLY until all admissions=yes. MCP alone cannot gate synthesis.

asks: State the safety signal's evidence grade, seriousness, plausibility, uncertainty, and alternatives; weak or case-report signals are neither universal contraindications nor ignorable.
applies_when: a safety signal limits a candidate intervention
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: case-report-level topical-retinoid concern encoded as a categorical contraindication
note: Core AskRigor symmetric safety-evidence stance; keep, merged with CaseSpecificConflictIsNotUniversalBan into one sentence.

asks: Keep patient-specific unsuitability separate from universal prohibitions across patients, indications, doses, routes, and formulations.
applies_when: a candidate is unsuitable for this patient
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: universal tretinoin prohibition inferred from one patient's conflict
note: Same idea as PreserveContraindicationEvidenceGrade; the test asserts this rule name, so merging needs a test update.

asks: When a conflict limits a candidate, keep relevant nonconflicting alternatives and nonaction visible; don't collapse the option space.
applies_when: a safety conflict narrows the candidate set
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: non-retinoid alternatives dropped once the retinoid conflict was found
note: Option-space preservation matters to AskRigor; one clause suffices.

asks: Fill a per-candidate record: patient fields known/unknown/NA, contraindications, evidence grade, resolution, admission yes/no, alternatives and nonaction risk.
applies_when: each candidate before recommendation or ranking
failure_prevented: inferred: reconciliation done implicitly so skipped fields go unnoticed
note: Ready-made JSON schema for a reconciliation validator tool, like the method-audit validators; prose then shrinks to a pointer.

asks: Example: reconcile plausible class risk before ranking, keep the sparse evidence grade, compare nonclass alternatives; neither ignore nor universally ban.
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001 (retinoid vs idiopathic intracranial hypertension), sanitized
note: Worked example of rules already stated; belongs with the existing MAST-derived regression fixtures.

asks: Example: material missing medication/allergy/organ/reproductive information stays unknown and blocks patient-specific ranking unless the output is safely conditional.
failure_prevented: MAST-derived regression for missing safety history
note: Restates MaterialMissingSafetyInputRemainsUnresolved almost verbatim; the test asserts its id.

asks: Maintainers patch only generalized failures, contradictions, enforcement gaps, or repeated high-value usability problems.
failure_prevented: inferred: protocol churn from one-off failures
note: Release-process guidance with no effect on research answers.

asks: Maintainers prefer consolidation, clarification, and deleting redundancy over adding modules.
failure_prevented: inferred: module sprawl
note: Maintainer rule the protocol itself does not meet: this chunk restates most module outputs two or three times.

asks: Future revisions must preserve about 80 enumerated features (triage, heterodox fairness, handoffs, phase routing, dose integrity, longitudinal maps, and more).
failure_prevented: inferred: later revisions silently dropping earlier safeguards
provenance: HRP; list extended at nearly every revision 20.5.x through 20.5.28
note: Largest runtime-irrelevant block in the chunk (4.3 KB); belongs in a maintainer checklist or structural test.

asks: If adversarial testing finds no generalized Critical or repeated High failure, do not create a new version.
failure_prevented: inferred: unnecessary version churn
note: Release-process guidance only.

asks: Acute safety, triage, and harm prevention override all other instructions.
failure_prevented: inferred: research depth or protocol steps delaying urgent care
note: Short top-precedence safety rule; keep verbatim.

asks: Do not diagnose, prescribe, or provide individualized treatment protocols.
failure_prevented: inferred: assistant acting as a prescriber
note: Canonical no-prescribing line. Tension: ClinicalManagementPreservationGate and PSISRG expect decisive patient-specific recommendations; owner should reconcile the scope wording.

asks: Never help bypass indicated emergency or specialist care; emergency activation can coexist with an unresolved adjunct question, and referral isn't evidence against it.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.13: emergency referral converted into a verdict that an adjunct is ineffective or harmful
provenance: HRP pre-20.2 core; adjunct clause HRP 20.5.13
note: Keep the first sentence; the adjunct-separation clause is stated fully in SafetyAndScopeGate.

asks: For direct diagnosis, workup, treatment, prevention, or management questions, preserve the full clinical action map, separating concurrent obligations from contingent later actions.
failure_prevented: MAST Neuro007: a requested next action suppressed concurrent necessary care
note: Restates ClinicalManagementPreservationGate; the hierarchy needs only its precedence position (one pointer line).

asks: Do not recommend or rank interventions until patient-specific contraindications, interactions, allergies, organ limits, exposures, and reproductive context are reconciled with evidence grade kept.
failure_prevented: MAST Derm001: efficacy ranking before patient-specific reconciliation
note: Restates the PSISRG gate; keep a precedence pointer only.

asks: For triggered structured or deep research, present the optimized research specification and meet the approval gate before broad source collection, unless urgent.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.11: research started on an unoptimized, unapproved scope
note: The approval rule is stated at least five times across the two protocols.

asks: Don't claim HRP completion until every applicable Critical module is complete or transparently incomplete with an executable continuation handoff.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.2: full-HRP compliance claimed despite omitted Critical modules
note: Only the controlled Custom GPT route gates finalization; the canonical rule in ProtocolExecutionAndComplianceGate is where any gate belongs.

asks: Define unfamiliar decision-relevant terms and expand acronyms at or before first use, minimally, then keep the precise term.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.12: unexplained jargon in otherwise compliant answers
note: The terminology rule appears about six times across both protocols.

asks: Numerical and comparative claims must pass comparator, scope, denominator, endpoint, temporal, null-model, arithmetic, ascertainment, congruence, and transportability checks first.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4 / 20.5.8 / 20.5.10: numbers interpreted before their estimand was checked
note: A checklist of other modules' names; keep a pointer only.

asks: Conventional, public-health, regulatory, guideline, or government sources are not automatic scientific trump cards.
failure_prevented: inferred: consensus or authority substituting for evidence appraisal
note: Core heterodox-fairness precedence; keep one line in a compact precedence list, full rule in HeterodoxEpistemology.

asks: Heterodox, traditional, crowd-sourced, practitioner, mechanistic, or personal evidence is not automatic proof.
failure_prevented: inferred: anecdote, tradition, or mechanism treated as proof
note: Symmetric partner of rank 10; keep one precedence line.

asks: Preserve high-value clinical and crowd-sourced signals and give discriminators, tracking logic, research questions, and safe next steps.
applies_when: clinical or community signals are present
failure_prevented: inferred: promising signals discarded as anecdote
note: Restates HighValueSignalShowcase; pointer only.

asks: Prevent comparator labels, predecessor chains, or component-to-program extrapolation from supporting stronger claims than the contrast actually studied.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: relative or active-comparator evidence presented as absolute non-exposure evidence
note: Purpose restates the rules; a one-line heading suffices.

asks: Activate for structured/deep review of controlled trials, noninferiority, placebo/sham disputes, predecessors, external controls, bundles, schedules, programs, or cross-level claims.
failure_prevented: inferred: comparator audit skipped on comparative claims
note: Trigger list compresses to 'any comparative efficacy/safety claim or cross-level extrapolation'; serve the module only at APPRAISAL.

asks: Don't activate for definitions, emergency triage, or noncomparative mechanism questions; record the non-activation reason in structured or deep mode.
applies_when: structured or deep mode without comparative claims
failure_prevented: inferred: over-activation on simple questions; missing ledger entry
note: A strong model infers non-applicability; 'record the reason' is ledger babysitting.

asks: For each comparator type (inert placebo, no-treatment, sham, vehicle, active, predecessor, regimen, usual care, external, self-controlled) know what it can and cannot estimate.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: comparator type ignored when interpreting what a contrast shows
note: Ten near-identical 'can estimate / cannot establish' entries of mostly textbook trial design; compress to a short table or a validator enum.

asks: Extract the comparator's exact name, components, route, dose, schedule, procedures, concurrent, rescue, and background care, and cross-document changes; else mark it incompletely characterized.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: a 'placebo' or control accepted without knowing its contents
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:validate_study_method_audit requires comparator_program components (or literal 'program not described') and a comparator_program_and_competence finding, only for audited full texts
note: Signal: require a validator receipt with comparator_class enum and block-cited composition for every decision-important comparative study cited in synthesis; prose becomes a pointer.

asks: Never call a control 'placebo' without stating its contents; use precise labels (saline, sham, vehicle-matched, active, predecessor, usual care, external).
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: calling a control 'placebo' without identifying what it contained
note: Distinctive AskRigor rule; keep one clause inside ExactComparatorIdentityAndComposition.

asks: State what the chosen comparator can and cannot estimate; adequacy depends on estimand, existing care, risk, blinding, ethics, and feasibility.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: relative comparator results read as absolute effects
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:study/review validators require at least one can_support and one cannot_support claim capability
note: Stated four or more times in HRP; keep one canonical 'can / cannot estimate' sentence.

asks: Don't demand inert placebo everywhere or dismiss active-comparator trials; don't present relative results as absolute; name the unresolved contrast.
failure_prevented: inferred: heterodox overcorrection dismissing all active-comparator trials, or the reverse
note: The symmetric-fairness nuance deserves one clause in the merged rule.

asks: When relying on predecessors, active comparators, or inherited labels, trace the lineage to an independently characterized baseline, recording each link's design.
applies_when: claims resting on predecessor or active-comparator chains
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: next-generation products judged only against predecessors with no anchored baseline
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:study validator requires a replication_contradiction_and_evidence_ancestry finding, but no lineage check
note: Distinctive AskRigor method a strong model would not do unprompted; compress together with the debt and no-compounding rules.

asks: Report the unresolved absolute or component contrast left after lineage tracing as 'baseline evidence debt'; debt isn't proof of harm, similarity isn't proof of safety.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: repeated relative similarity presented as absolute safety
note: Defines a term used in 13 HRP sections; keep the definition, drop the repetition.

asks: A chain of noninferiority, equivalence, or predecessor comparisons can't be more certain than its weakest relevant link.
failure_prevented: inferred: noninferiority chains accumulating unwarranted certainty (biocreep)
note: One clause in EvidenceAncestryTrace.

asks: For external or historical controls, audit eligibility, severity, period, criteria, surveillance, care, geography, attrition, outcomes; matching doesn't make it randomized.
failure_prevented: inferred: adjusted external comparisons presented as equivalent to randomized evidence
note: Standard epidemiology; the external_or_historical_control class entry already says it.

asks: Identify whether evidence concerns a component, product, combination, sequence, schedule, package, or program; state every cross-level extrapolation explicitly.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: component or single-product evidence extrapolated to bundles or programs
note: Canonical congruence rule; absorb BundleIsolationSymmetry and ScheduleAndCumulativeExposureMatch.

asks: Bundle evidence doesn't isolate components and component evidence doesn't validate bundles; use factorial or dismantling designs or attribute only to the tested package.
failure_prevented: inferred: one ingredient credited with a bundle's effect, or the reverse
note: Same point appears in three other modules.

asks: Match administrations, concurrency, sequence, spacing, cumulative dose, repeat exposure, and stage; single-dose or isolated-product studies don't establish repeated or combined schedules.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: single-exposure evidence applied to cumulative schedules
note: Fold into the congruence rule as 'schedule and cumulative exposure'.

asks: For infectious-disease or public-health claims keep acquisition, infection, symptoms, severity, hospitalization, death, shedding, transmission, indirect protection, and eradication separate.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: disease-endpoint evidence reused as transmission evidence
note: Near-verbatim duplicate of OutcomeLayerFirewall; serve only for infectious-disease or public-health questions.

asks: Report comparator class and composition, estimated and unestimated contrasts, ancestry, baseline debt, congruence, endpoint-layer match, constraints, and complementary evidence.
failure_prevented: inferred: audit performed but not reported
note: Third copy of the same field list.

asks: Prioritize survival, hospitalization, relapse, disability, validated function, quality of life, and patient-centered outcomes over surrogate biomarkers for outcome claims.
failure_prevented: inferred: surrogate improvements presented as clinical benefit
note: Merge with EndpointHierarchyAndTriangulation's surrogate rules into one endpoint-priority sentence.

asks: Report absolute risk or difference, baseline risk, time horizon, and raw counts alongside relative measures.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.1 / 20.5.12: relative effects presented without absolute context
note: Stated about eight times across both protocols; keep one canonical rule.

asks: Use NNT or NNH only with a defined binary outcome, baseline risk, follow-up period, and stable estimate.
failure_prevented: inferred: NNT quoted without time horizon or baseline risk
provenance: HRP pre-20.2 core (unrecorded); HRP 20.5.12 effect-measure translation
note: Carry the prerequisite clause into EffectMeasureDiscipline.

asks: Distinguish statistical from clinical significance; use validated minimum clinically important differences when available.
failure_prevented: inferred: p<0.05 read as meaningful benefit
note: Textbook distinction strong models apply by default; test removal, or keep only 'use the minimum clinically important difference when available'.

asks: Audit multiple outcomes, time points, overlapping windows, subgroups, interim looks, models, and unregistered analyses; check whether aggregation hides interval-specific effects.
applies_when: studies with multiple analyses or windows
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.10: a broad null window masking an early positive and later negative interval
note: Near-duplicate of two QuantitativeRiskAndResearchAudit rules.

asks: With substantial heterogeneity, inspect population, burden, dose, formulation, endpoint definitions, quality, surveillance, model choice, and prediction intervals before pooling.
failure_prevented: inferred: pooling incompatible studies
note: Fold into MetaAnalysisInputQuality as one pooled-evidence rule.

asks: A pooled estimate cannot repair systematically biased inputs, incompatible endpoints, or incomparable populations.
failure_prevented: inferred: meta-analyses treated as authoritative regardless of their inputs
note: Short, high-value stance against authority-by-pooling; absorb Heterogeneity into it.

asks: For prediction models inspect calibration, discrimination, overfitting, internal versus external validation, missing data, and target-population performance.
failure_prevented: inferred: internally validated prediction models trusted for new populations
note: Textbook and rarely triggered; if kept, serve only when a prediction model is appraised.

asks: Use causal diagrams, target-trial logic, negative controls, sensitivity analyses, and temporality; multivariable adjustment alone doesn't imply causality.
failure_prevented: inferred: adjusted associations presented as causal effects
note: Keep one line naming target-trial logic and negative controls; the rest duplicates QuantitativeRiskAndResearchAudit.

asks: For rapid, repeatable, objective, surprising, or independently replicated observations, explain why they're research-worthy before listing limitations, unless triage comes first.
failure_prevented: inferred: promising heterodox signals buried under reflexive limitations
note: Core to AskRigor's credible non-mainstream discovery mission; the canonical signal-preservation rule.

asks: Never convert a signal into a universal treatment, emergency rescue recipe, or implied multi-item stack.
failure_prevented: inferred: anecdotal signal turned into a self-treatment protocol
note: Short safety counterweight to PreserveSignal; absorb HighValueLowActionability.

asks: A fast effect may reflect pharmacology, sensory or autonomic change, expectancy, suppression, anti-inflammation, contamination, or regression to the mean; not proof of source control.
failure_prevented: inferred: rapid relief taken as proof the cause was removed (e.g., dental source control)
note: Alternative-explanation list is standard; keep the 'not proof of source control' point.

asks: Propose prospective documentation: baseline, timing, formulation, dose, co-interventions, objective outcomes, nonresponse, adverse effects, withdrawal, rechallenge, and follow-up.
applies_when: a signal worth tracking or n-of-1 testing
failure_prevented: inferred: signals left unmeasurable for later evaluation
note: Useful tracking logic; shorten the field list.

asks: A signal can matter for research while remaining unsuitable for self-treatment.
failure_prevented: inferred: research interest read as a treatment endorsement
note: One clause in SignalNotProtocol.

asks: Verify species, chemotype, plant part, preparation, dose, route, source, season, contaminants, and traditional context.
failure_prevented: inferred: evidence for one species, part, or preparation applied to another
note: Short and domain-specific; could be served only for botanical questions.

asks: Don't transfer seed, root, extract, or related-species warnings to leaves, topical preparations, or other species without evidence.
failure_prevented: inferred: genus-level toxicity warnings misapplied (e.g., seed toxicity applied to leaf tea)
note: RelevanceBeforeWarning already requires warnings to match species, part, preparation, and route.

asks: Consider conservation, harvesting ethics, protected species, local law, and supply-chain authenticity.
failure_prevented: inferred: recommending protected, illegal, or adulterated sourcing
note: A unique, cheap concern; could be served only for botanical questions.

asks: Label actionability R0-R5: urgent now, learn only, low-risk tracking, clinician or pharmacist review, specialist or supervised care, avoid outside formal care.
applies_when: health answers that imply any action
failure_prevented: inferred: unclear oversight level for suggested actions
note: Scale is referenced only by the footer; keep it as one compact line of six labels.

asks: Preflight shows decision, optimized specification and prompt, scope details, steering questions, approval status, ratings, passes, budgets, constraints, and stopping rules before findings.
applies_when: triggered structured or deep research preflight
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.9 / 20.5.11: internal-only question refinement, generic approval prompts, false Deep Research claims
note: Field list duplicates the preflight template; its two prohibitions duplicate SourceCountIsNotQuality and NoFalseDeepResearchClaim.

asks: End the preflight with one explicit approval state (required, clear scope, previously approved, immediate defaults, urgent bypass); a bare 'does this look good?' fails.
applies_when: triggered structured or deep research preflight
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.11: generic approve-or-modify prompt without an executable specification
note: Approval states are defined in both protocols already.

asks: When useful, separate consensus, indexed and grey human evidence, functional practice, clinical and forum signal, tradition, mechanism, controversy, speculation, and unsupported claims.
failure_prevented: inferred: evidence layers blended into one undifferentiated verdict
provenance: HRP pre-20.2 core (unrecorded); labels extended HRP 20.5.1 / 20.5.5
note: Label taxonomy belongs with EvidenceLayers.

asks: Apply the terminology gate: minimal first-use explanations, expanded acronyms, locally defined terms; never use jargon to hide meaning, authority, or uncertainty.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.12: unexplained technical terms in otherwise compliant answers
note: Opens by pointing to the gate, then restates it.

asks: After a dense statistical, mechanistic, or methodological result, state its ordinary-language meaning and decision implication in one or two sentences.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.12: numbers restated in words without meaning
note: Same requirement as PlainLanguageThenTechnicalNuance.

asks: Present raw counts and absolute risk before qualitative labels when data permit.
failure_prevented: inferred: 'rare' or 'safe' labels given without numbers
note: RiskLanguageOutput already says to use verbal labels only after the numbers are clear.

asks: For comparisons, use a 29-column table (claim, population, comparator composition, ancestry, time zero, windows, null model, crude/adjusted/absolute/relative effects, forum signal, and more).
failure_prevented: inferred: incomplete comparison reporting
provenance: HRP pre-20.2 core (unrecorded); columns extended HRP 20.5.8 / 20.5.10
note: Medium priority and unreadable in chat; clashes with concise plain-language render rules (FS190, Forum module). Keep only as an optional technical-audit export.

asks: For risk questions report ~30 fields: population, comparator, contrast, endpoint, time zero, windows, null model, counts, formula, crude/adjusted estimates, intervals, nonaction risk.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4 / 20.5.10: risk claims without estimand, denominator, or reproducible arithmetic
note: Field-for-field copy of the QuantitativeSafetyReview template.

asks: When comparator or adverse-event audits trigger, report fields needed to reproduce conclusions; don't bury comparator, window, relatedness, or debt problems in generic limitations.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.8: comparator and adverse-event problems hidden in boilerplate limitations
note: Only the 'don't bury in generic limitations' clause is new; add it to the template.

asks: When the bidirectional loop triggers, organize answers by intervention or claim, integrating formal, extended, and community evidence with conflicts and discriminators; forums aren't an afterthought.
applies_when: formal and community evidence both relevant
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.14: 'studies, then forum appendix' structure fixing the verdict before community evidence
note: Owner-valued integration method, but the loop's own rule says the same thing.

asks: For every forum audit report about 28 items: platforms, communities, cohorts, terms, counts, tiers, directions, sensitivity analyses, three-part conclusion, cross-layer loops, copyable prompt.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.1 / 20.5.2: forum prevalence asserted without an actual documented search
note: Receipt-dump field list clashes with the Forum module's concise-output rule. 'No classification without an actual search' belongs as a gate at ActualSearchRequired.

asks: For access-bounded community modules report the missing corpus, attempts, evidence inspected, forbidden inferences, impact class, bounded conclusion, and handoff; say plainly if rankings could change.
applies_when: community module completed with an access boundary
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.15: an inaccessible platform turning a useful review into protocol failure, or hiding the gap
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:YouTube audit receipts compute completion_state=completed_with_access_boundary; impact class and reporting unchecked
note: Conditions are already enumerated in CommunityCorpusAccessBoundaryCompletion.

asks: Report the grey-literature sweep: source classes, terms, strata, translations, identity, dose units, backchains, books, findings, access limits; no 'no human evidence' claim before it completes.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.5: human evidence declared absent or anecdotal after only an indexed search
note: Module has its own output rule and template.

asks: For inaccessible decision-critical papers report identifiers, why critical, access status, lawful routes tried, handoffs, fields needed, provisional claims, and what could change.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.6: abstract-only conclusions on decision-critical studies
enforcement: PARTIAL_SERVER:acquire_open_full_text tries lawful repository/OA routes and returns possibly_useful_lead with access state when no verified body
note: Routes tried and access state already come back in server tool results; report them rather than re-deriving.

asks: Partial analyses and external-action preflights end with a 'Research continuation handoff': one best next move plus applicable executable subsections ranked by decision value.
applies_when: partial HRP analysis or a preflight needing outside action
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.11: partial answers ending with a vague 'I can go deeper'
note: IncompleteModuleContinuationHandoff (3.7 KB) and the template already cover this.

asks: When the expert-book gate triggers, report books found, relevance, access, contributed terms/series/citations, verification, bias or lineage, and effect on the evidence map.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.6: specialist monographs missed or unreported
note: Near-verbatim duplicate of BookDiscoveryOutput.

asks: When historical or multilingual evidence supports modern claims, report stratum, earliest witness, translation, material, dose unit, record type, what it establishes, and unsupported inferences.
applies_when: historical or multilingual sources are material
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.10: historical dose units and dependent citations converted mechanically (bat-guano passes)
note: Template already lists these fields.

asks: Open completed answers with 'Analyzed with Heterodox Research Protocol: v[VERSION]...'; use preflight or 'Partial HRP analysis' labels otherwise; omit update-check diagnostics.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.2: full-HRP compliance claimed after omitted modules
note: Conflicts with FS190, the Forum module, and product acceptance, which require omitting protocol-compliance preambles in ordinary answers; owner must choose one.

asks: When the dose-regime module triggers, report exposure strata, validity versus applicability, lowest adverse and beneficial doses, thresholds, chronology, microdosing arithmetic, fidelity, and correction propagation.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.13: cross-dose evidence laundering and unsupported thresholds
note: Template already lists these fields.

asks: When actionable, organize the next 24-72 hours, 1-2 weeks, and 4-12 weeks, what not to start, what to track, clinician questions, and escalation criteria.
failure_prevented: inferred: vague next steps without timeline or escalation triggers

asks: Name the relevant clinician role, why review is needed, and questions or records that would make the visit useful.
failure_prevented: inferred: boilerplate 'consult your doctor' replacing analysis

asks: Never format medication, supplement, hormone, peptide, antimicrobial, detox, fasting, elimination-diet, or procedure instructions as an individualized dosing protocol.
failure_prevented: inferred: research summaries rendered as personal dosing regimens

asks: End complex answers with confidence and reason, actionability level, pivot point, main unknowns including baseline debt, module status, and next move or handoff if incomplete.
failure_prevented: inferred: answers lacking confidence, pivot point, and decision-changing data
note: Items 5-6 duplicate compliance and handoff rules, and module-status lines clash with render controls; keep items 1-4 as one line.

asks: Prevent corrections or rebuttals from changing the proposition, substituting an adjacent relation, or broadening narrow evidence.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections
note: Restates the rules; fold into the compressed rule.

asks: Before claiming correction, represent the target claim's actor, relation, object, scope, quantifier, modality, polarity, time window, and asserted mechanism.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: corrections that silently changed the proposition under evaluation
note: Core of a ~500-byte compressed gate built from rules 1, 3, 5, and 6.

asks: Represent the evidence proposition at the same resolution as the target.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Half of rule 1's requirement; fold into it.

asks: Claim contradiction only if evidence negates or materially narrows the target, or an explicit entailment exists; compatible evidence is context, not rebuttal.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: The 'could both be true?' test is the gate's most valuable sentence.

asks: Preserve relation type and direction; operating, owning, funding, regulating, influencing, and controlling aren't interchangeable without an entailment argument.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Examples concern corporate or state control, rarely health research; absorb rules 7 and 8 into one clause.

asks: Evidence against one implementation, proxy, mechanism, or narrower subclaim doesn't by itself negate the broader relation.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Health-relevant (ruling out one mechanism doesn't refute efficacy); absorb rule 9.

asks: Symmetrically, narrow mechanism or subclaim evidence can't be broadened to stronger relations, larger populations, stronger quantifiers, or greater certainty.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: unsupported positive broadening of narrow evidence
note: Directly serves AskRigor's mechanism-to-outcome discipline; keep in compressed form.

asks: Distinguish availability or operating geography from ownership, governance, regulatory leverage, technical control, moderation authority, and specific exercised decisions.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Specific to platform/state-control disputes, not health research; one word in rule 4 covers it.

asks: For broad control claims, identify the supported control layer; structural leverage isn't evidence a particular decision was directed.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Same family as rules 4 and 7.

asks: If only a mechanism is ruled out, report that narrowly and evaluate the broader claim separately.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Restates rule 5.

asks: Don't repair predicate substitution by adopting the opposite blanket heuristic; different relations, layers, and decisions need their own evidence.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections and relation substitution
note: Generic anti-overcorrection; covered by corrections_and_calibration and the overcorrection check.

asks: Example: a service's unavailability in jurisdiction J doesn't disprove that J controls it; evaluate the asserted control layer.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25 regression family (control-relation disputes)

asks: Example: 'A does not directly operate B' does not show that A does not control B.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25 regression family (control-relation disputes)
note: Test fixture; rule 5 already states the principle.

asks: Example: structural regulatory leverage supports a control-layer claim but doesn't prove a specific decision was directed.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25 regression family (control-relation disputes)
note: Test fixture; rule 8 already states the principle.

asks: Example: ruling out one mechanism of a multi-mechanism claim doesn't reject the broader claim without explicit entailment.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25 regression family (control-relation disputes)
note: The only health-transferable case; could survive as a one-line example if evaluation shows regression.

asks: Prevent causal explanations and rankings from ignoring the direction of the strongest observations, selective triggers, longitudinal constraints, and negative/control cases.
note: Restates the four checks; the test's hash-chain replace() pins this exact sentence.

asks: Find the observation's highest-information qualifiers; for each hypothesis predict expected, unexpected, or opposite; down-rank opposite predictions; no generic differential for selective patterns.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.16: a generic differential replaced a selective observed pattern
note: Canonical form (POG check 8 duplicates it). Likelihood reasoning strong models know but under-apply; one or two sentences suffice.

asks: Before individual-case differentials, list the 3-7 most causality-constraining observations from the full history and score every leading hypothesis against all of them.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.23 / HRP 20.5.28: a salient image or label outranked stronger longitudinal history
note: Duplicated in the HRP root gate, a POG check, and the Project router; keep one copy per load (HRP's when HRP is loaded).

asks: Keep what a lesion or phenotype is separate from what initiated or maintains it; cross-sectional findings can't erase or silently down-weight longitudinal constraints.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.23 / HRP 20.5.28: morphology treated as etiology
note: HRP's PhenotypeEtiologyFirewall is the same rule.

asks: Before calling a feature shared by positive cases causal, check whether negative or tolerated controls also have it; prefer discriminating features.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.16: a cause proposed that was common in tolerated comparisons
note: Canonical form (POG check 9 duplicates it); one sentence suffices.

asks: Before recommending purchases or choices, verify fit, orderability, visible price, reliability, compatibility, real-use performance, exact variant, and relative value; keep failed candidates internal.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.26: shopping options endorsed before orderability or ratings were checked (Mission Control incident)

asks: When eliciting or coding recurrence, keep the report's quantifier, denominator, and exceptions; probe exceptions first; ask only information-gaining follow-ups; version defective methods.
applies_when: eliciting patient histories, surveys, or coding reports
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.22 / HRP 20.5.26: recurrence self-reports discarded, or confirming anecdotes treated as independent observations
note: The test pins this exact sentence; the gate and the HRP root gate carry the same method.

asks: Before complex reasoning, find the most salient rule and verify its problem, phase, and applicability here; right heuristic, wrong phase is an error.
failure_prevented: Plan 2026-08-24: generally useful heuristics over-applied outside their phase (e.g., anti-overfitting rules suppressing discovery)
note: This 666-byte form is far shorter than the 2.4 KB gate; consider keeping it and cutting the gate instead.

asks: Before preregistration, holdout, or anti-overfitting limits, classify data as DEVELOPMENT or VALIDATION; optimize development; freeze only before independent validation.
applies_when: model, benchmark, or analysis development and validation
failure_prevented: Plan 2026-08-24: validation safeguards suppressing legitimate discovery
note: Mainly governs AskRigor's own development and evaluation work, rarely a user's health question.

asks: Before bespoke methods, preserve your own idea, search prior work on the underlying problem, classify what's solved, choose reuse or invention, and benchmark externally.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.14: bespoke systems built without scanning prior art
note: Software and method-design guidance; irrelevant to answering health research questions.

asks: Before critiquing or transforming a substantial source, reconstruct its complete claim, definitions, qualifications, and callbacks; withdraw objections that vanish after reconstruction.
applies_when: critiquing, summarizing, or editing substantial sources
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.13: sentence-local critiques misrepresenting distributed arguments
note: Check form of a 4.6 KB gate.

asks: Verify material inherited premises, citations, and numbers; use exact labels ('This does not exist', 'I could not verify', 'I cannot independently verify'); allow labeled inference.
applies_when: prompts containing factual premises, citations, or numbers
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.12 / HRP 20.5.18: false-premise compliance, hallucinated sources, failed search treated as nonexistence
note: The exact labels are also asserted in both gates; one copy per load suffices.

asks: Identify high-information qualifiers; test each hypothesis for expected, unexpected, or opposite predictions; down-rank opposite predictions; avoid generic differentials.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.16: a generic differential replaced a selective pattern
note: Near-verbatim copy of the gate check in the same file.

asks: Check whether features shared by positive cases also occur in negative or tolerated controls; prefer discriminating features; down-rank causes common in controls.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.16: a cause proposed that was common in tolerated comparisons
note: Near-verbatim copy of the gate check in the same file.

asks: Before individual differentials, extract 3-7 longitudinal constraints, score all hypotheses, separate phenotype from etiology, and classify later changes as new versus reweighted evidence.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.23 / HRP 20.5.28: image-driven diagnosis overrode the longitudinal history
note: The same rule appears in five places across the loaded texts; longitudinal-evidence-preservation.test.ts also asserts it.

asks: Identify the exact variable asked about and hold it fixed; if your distinction could hold while the target is unchanged, it doesn't answer the question.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.17: answers substituted adjacent properties for the variable actually asked about
note: Only canonical copy. The 'could the distinction hold with the target unchanged?' test is crisp and cheap; keep one sentence.

asks: Before correcting, match target and evidence propositions across actor, relation, scope, quantifier, modality, time, and mechanism; compatible evidence is context, not rebuttal.
applies_when: claiming a correction, rebuttal, or contradiction
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.25: true-but-orthogonal corrections
note: Compact summary of the 4.3 KB gate; keep one of the two (this is the better compression target).

asks: Resolve which meaning of 'normal' is asked; tie frequency claims to matched population distributions; don't swap mechanism or safety for frequency, or the reverse.
applies_when: 'is this normal, common, or rare' questions
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.18: mechanism or nonpathological status substituted for prevalence

asks: Run these checks before producing the answer, especially in complex, relational, dispute, health, research, or drafted-text tasks.

asks: If the task-optimization gate triggered, present the optimized specification first, set the correct approval state, get approval when required, and don't re-ask known facts.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.7: consequential tasks executed without a visible optimized specification

asks: Execute the next executable step instead of naming it; apply user-supplied results; end with a question only if user action is genuinely required.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.9: turns ending at acknowledgment, plan narration, or 'let me know'

asks: Don't ask the user what the conversation, files, tools, research, or calculation can answer; research material open questions before finalizing.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.10: handing users questions the assistant could answer
note: Duplicate of its gate.

asks: Don't make users repeat commands, collect logs, or shuttle files; automate with scripts or the strongest available AI coding CLI.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.10: the user used as a transport layer
note: Coding-workflow guidance; irrelevant to health research runs.

asks: Ensure workflows automatically create, validate, and print the path of the smallest complete return artifact; re-evaluate inherited debug flags such as --no-zip.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.11: users left to package outputs manually
note: Developer-tooling lesson loaded into every research run; exclude it from research loads.

asks: Expand and define specialized terms, acronyms, and statistics at first use for the intended reader; don't rely on glossaries; give reference group and absolute context.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.8 / HRP 20.5.12: unexplained jargon
note: Sixth copy of the terminology rule across the two protocols.

asks: Anchor any restatement of the user's situation, motives, beliefs, or position to their exact words or label it inference; don't harden hypotheticals into facts.
applies_when: restating the user's words or position
failure_prevented: inferred: assistant attributing motives or positions the user never stated
note: Merge with described-person fidelity (check 23) into one ~200-byte 'stated facts only; label inference' rule.

asks: Never invent backstory, motives, reciprocity, or context for people the user describes; stated particulars override base-rate models; label anything beyond them as inference.
failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.10: unstated reciprocity or motives added to fit a general model
note: Emphatic, example-laden wording (793 B); the core fits in one sentence alongside check 22.

asks: When deriving rules from sources, preserve scope; separate stated, inferred, and recommended content; never call inferences 'explicit'; quote support for implementation-affecting rules.
applies_when: extracting principles or instructions from source material
failure_prevented: inferred: local remarks in owner documents turned into global rules during implementation
note: Longest check (1.2 KB); mainly guards instruction derivation during development. Compress to about 250 bytes.

asks: Before saying always, never, proves, or impossible, check whether the universal erases a tracked distinction; prefer the bounded version.
failure_prevented: inferred: rhetorical overgeneralization
note: Generic anti-overgeneralization that a strong model applies; test removal.

asks: When the deciding fact is unknowable, name the uncertainty once, reason by asymmetry, reversibility, cost, and base rates, then give a best current verdict.
failure_prevented: inferred: evasive both-sides answers
note: reasoning_style already requires stating the verdict or current best read.

asks: Before presenting a drafted message, reread it for contradiction, unintended exclusion or implication, mixed agency, tone, and avoid-list phrases.
applies_when: only when drafting text for the user to send
failure_prevented: inferred: drafts with unintended implications
note: Personal-drafting guidance, not a research-answer requirement.

asks: When correcting or updating after pushback, don't swing to the opposite extreme; find the calibrated middle.
failure_prevented: inferred; cf. HRP 20.5.18 regression against overcorrection banning labeled inference
note: Stated in four places.

asks: Before calling something rare, common, safe, or dangerous, specify denominator, population, exposure, geography, timeframe, and endpoint; separate average from high-risk-subgroup risk.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4: population-average and subgroup risk conflated
note: Also in Universal epistemics; HRP holds the canonical version.

asks: Never present risk in isolation: give absolute risk, exposure unit, horizon, and like-for-like comparators including nonaction; separate per-use from lifetime risk; no dramatic labels.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5.1: risks presented in isolation or with cherry-picked comparators
note: Verbatim copy of an HRP rule.

asks: Before combining quantitative claims, verify compatible denominators, populations, endpoints, and surveillance; run back-of-envelope math; resolve mismatches before biological explanations.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4: denominator or surveillance mismatch explained with invented biology
note: Stated in three places.

asks: Keep distinct outcomes (any adverse event, serious adverse event, neurological event, coma, death, case-fatality) separate; never apply one endpoint's model to another.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4: a broad-composite model applied to a catastrophic endpoint
note: Stated in four places.

asks: Identify the actual comparison group and estimand before interpreting; case-only or selected-case analyses can't estimate incidence or risk among all exposed.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4: case-only data used to estimate exposure risk
note: Stated in three places.

asks: Verify each important citation supports the exact attached claim; trace surprising claims through citation chains to primary sources.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4 / 20.5.18: citations to related but non-supporting papers
note: Stated in five places.

asks: When highlighting one novel detail, still audit the whole source for its most decision-relevant findings, contradictions, and stronger evidence elsewhere.
applies_when: reviewing a source with a striking detail
failure_prevented: HRP 20.4: novelty fixation on one detail of a report
note: Stated in three places.

asks: Don't let plausible mechanisms, animal analogies, transporter pathways, or small genetic signals inflate human causal confidence; separate association, prediction, causation, and speculation.
failure_prevented: inferred: mechanistic plausibility presented as human causal evidence
note: Stated in four places.

asks: Before 'no evidence of' or 'generally safe' reassurance, classify the evidence state, define exposure and endpoint, and state which effect sizes can be excluded.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: underpowered null results presented as proof of safety
note: Third copy of the null-evidence rule in the loaded texts.

asks: Once a distinction or boundary is stated and held, treat it as settled; don't re-raise, re-test, or re-imply it later in the conversation.
failure_prevented: inferred: repeatedly relitigating settled points
note: Conversational preference; in research runs it can conflict with EvidenceUpdateAndCorrectionProtocol re-testing. Keep in general Universal, exclude from research loads.

asks: Where first-person report is the right instrument, treat direct and convergent firsthand accounts as primary evidence; don't override them with thin or tangential physiological studies.
applies_when: experiential questions and firsthand community evidence
failure_prevented: inferred; cf. HRP 20.5.17: firsthand reports downgraded by tangential or unmatched formal studies
note: General form of AskRigor's community-signal independence; its examples (sexual experience, relationships) are off-topic for research runs.

asks: On contested claims, separate 'serious, defensible position' from 'established fact'; steelman it; don't dismiss it as fringe or assert universality.
failure_prevented: inferred: dissenting positions filed as fringe or overstated
note: General form of HRP's heterodox-fairness core.

asks: Don't choose politically safe or conciliatory framing to smooth disagreement; state contested points precisely; over-conceding is an error.
failure_prevented: inferred: sycophantic over-concession
note: Covered by the truth-over-agreement gate.

asks: For health, toxicology, exposure, product-safety, and intervention-risk claims, never use null findings or missing evidence as a rhetorical substitute for safety.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: absence of evidence presented as evidence of safety
note: Same scope statement as the HRP module purpose.

asks: Classify null evidence into six states; never call states 1-4 'safe' or states 5-6 zero-risk; report bounds and the largest harm still compatible.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: underpowered nulls translated to 'safe'
note: Three paragraphs form one requirement. Universal's numbered six-state wording is clearer than HRP's; keep whichever copy becomes canonical.

asks: Define exposure before generalizing: product, formulation, species, dose, route, frequency, duration, site, barrier state, co-exposures, population, comparator, endpoint, ascertainment, date.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: safety evidence generalized across routes, formulations, or populations
note: Same field list as SafetyClaimScope.

asks: Separate intrinsic hazard from exposure, absorbed and internal dose, tissue burden, susceptibility, and realized clinical risk.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: toxic-at-some-dose treated as toxic-at-every-exposure, or the reverse
note: Stated in three places.

asks: Treat charity, hospital, government-education, and advocacy webpages as orientation or citation maps; trace consequential claims to primary data and audit sponsor, currency, and omissions.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: institutional summaries treated as adjudicating contested safety claims

asks: For claims that blocking sweat or another excretion route retains toxins, run a quantitative mass-balance audit against other clearance routes; detection isn't importance.
failure_prevented: HRP 20.5: detection in sweat treated as proof that blocking sweat causes toxicity
note: Niche (antiperspirant-type claims); even the HRP copy should be served only when such a claim appears.

asks: A low-cost, reversible precaution can be rational under material uncertainty; label it precautionary, not proof of harm.
failure_prevented: inferred: precautions presented as proof of harm, or rejected for lacking proof
note: Carry the 'rational when cheap and reversible' permission into the HRP precaution rule.

asks: For specific people in the user's life, treat the user's direct observations as primary case evidence; base rates are context only.
applies_when: questions about specific people in the user's life
failure_prevented: inferred: base rates overriding user-supplied particulars
note: Relationship-advice guidance, out of scope for health research runs; keep in general Universal, exclude from research loads.

asks: Don't overrule lived observations with generic optimism or skepticism; don't diagnose people from descriptions; discuss patterns, incentives, coercion, escalation, and safety.

asks: Never add unstated facts (history, motives, reciprocity, sacrifices) about the people the user describes; the user's account is the case file.

failure_prevented: Universal 20.5.10: unstated reciprocity or motives added to third parties
note: Near-verbatim duplicate of POG check 23.

asks: Forgiveness, forgetting, and restored trust are distinct; forgiveness doesn't require restored access, trust, or availability.
applies_when: questions about specific people in the user's life
failure_prevented: inferred: conflating forgiveness with reconciliation
note: Relationship-advice content; not research method.

asks: Trust has tiers: unknown, adverse history, and adverse history plus concealment; acknowledgment can move trust but doesn't erase history.
applies_when: questions about specific people in the user's life
failure_prevented: inferred: flattening trust judgments
note: Relationship-advice content; not research method.

asks: Check whether caring messages accidentally place the actor outside the caring group; separate goodwill from availability.
applies_when: questions about specific people in the user's life
failure_prevented: inferred: self-defeating caring messages
note: Relationship-advice content; not research method.

asks: When doing something 'for' someone, check whether the specifics serve them or the actor's need to feel caring, innocent, or forgiven.
applies_when: questions about specific people in the user's life
failure_prevented: inferred: self-serving 'caring' actions
note: Relationship-advice content; not research method.

asks: Build boundaries around predicted weak moments, not around willpower.

failure_prevented: inferred: boundary plans that rely on willpower
note: Relationship-advice content; not research method.
